processes.title: Foreigners questioned in a criminal case

steps.title: Consultation and checking your status of stay
steps.desc: A managing partner personally hears the allegations and the details of the request to appear, and checks your status of stay and its expiry date using your passport and residence card (외국인등록증). Consultations are available in English and Chinese.
steps.tip: If you get advice before setting the date to appear, we can arrange the interpreter and our attendance at the same time.

steps.title: Requesting an interpreter and practicing for questioning
steps.desc: We tell the investigator in advance which language you need an interpreter for, and we practice questioning with likely questions. We make sure you do not fill in what you cannot remember with guesses.
steps.tip: The police must provide interpretation in a language you understand (Police Investigation Rules Article 91(1)).

steps.title: Sitting in on questioning
steps.desc: We go into the interview room with you, check that the interpreted questions and answers match, and object on the spot to leading or improper questions. Before you sign, we check the statement record again through the interpreter.
steps.tip: Ask for the statement record to be read back to you through the interpreter, and correct anything recorded differently before you sign.

steps.title: Written opinions and responding to the decision
steps.desc: If you dispute the allegations, we submit a written opinion organizing the evidence. If you admit them, we submit evidence of compensation to the victim and of your life in Korea to the police and prosecutor. We also explain how the level of the outcome affects your stay.
steps.period: If you receive a summary order (약식명령), you can request a formal trial within 7 days of being notified (Criminal Procedure Act Article 453)
steps.tip: Even if the case ends in a suspended indictment or a decision not to refer it to prosecutors, investigation history records remain.

steps.title: Connecting to immigration procedures
steps.desc: Once a decision or judgment is issued, we prepare for requests to appear at the immigration office, extension reviews and deportation procedures. If needed, we continue on to objections and administrative lawsuits.
steps.tip: Prison wardens must notify the immigration office of foreigners whose release has been decided (Immigration Act Article 84(2)).

processes.summary: For foreign suspects, procedures such as interpretation and consular notification are added, and the outcome carries over to immigration review. Here are the steps in order, from the request to appear to the immigration procedures.

processes.title: When you receive a departure order or deportation order

steps.title: Checking the type of decision and the dates
steps.desc: We check whether the document you received is a departure recommendation (출국권고서), a departure order (출국명령서) or a deportation order (강제퇴거명령서), and write down the date you received it and the departure deadline. The available procedures and deadlines differ by type.
steps.period: The departure deadline in a departure order is set within 30 days of the issue date (Enforcement Rules Article 65)
steps.tip: Write down the date you received it. The deadline for an objection is counted from that day.

steps.title: Objection
steps.desc: For a deportation order, an objection is submitted to the Minister of Justice through the immigration office within 7 days of receiving the order. If there are special reasons you need to stay in Korea, we also request special permission to stay (체류허가 특례).
steps.period: 7 days from the day you received the deportation order (Immigration Act Article 60(1))
steps.tip: If you previously held Korean nationality or have special reasons to stay, we also seek special permission to stay (Article 61).

steps.title: Responding to detention
steps.desc: If you are held in an immigration detention center, we request a review of the detention or apply for temporary release from detention to the Immigration Detention Committee. We prepare the security deposit, a guarantor and proof of housing.
steps.period: The Immigration Detention Committee decides within 3 weeks, and this can be extended once by up to 2 weeks (Enforcement Decree Articles 70 and 79-2)
steps.tip: The security deposit is set at KRW 20 million or less (Article 65).

steps.title: Administrative lawsuit and stay of execution
steps.desc: We file a lawsuit to cancel the decision within 90 days of the day you learned of it, and if departure or removal is imminent, we also apply for a stay of execution. We use evidence to show harm that would be hard to undo, such as family ties, illness or ongoing court cases.
steps.period: 90 days from the day you learned of the decision (Administrative Litigation Act Article 20)
steps.tip: Filing a lawsuit does not suspend the decision, so we also apply for a stay of execution.

steps.title: Wrapping up based on the outcome
steps.desc: If the decision stands, we settle money owed to you, property and ongoing cases before you leave, and check in advance anything that could cause problems if you want to enter Korea again.
steps.tip: If you appoint a representative, money owed to you and your cases can be settled even after you leave Korea.

processes.summary: The ways and deadlines to challenge the decision depend on whether you received a departure order or a deportation order, and whether you also received a detention order.

processes.title: When your extension or change of status is refused

steps.title: Checking the refusal notice
steps.desc: We check the reasons for refusal and the departure deadline. In principle, the departure deadline is set within 14 days of the notice's issue date. If a change of status was refused, we also check whether you can stay for the remaining period under your existing status.
steps.period: In principle, the departure deadline is within 14 days of the issue date (Enforcement Decree of the Immigration Act Article 33(2))

steps.title: Choosing how to challenge it
steps.desc: If the refusal was due to missing documents, it may be faster to add them and reapply. If the problem is a discretionary judgment or a factual error, we prepare an administrative appeal or administrative lawsuit.
steps.period: Both administrative appeals and administrative lawsuits: 90 days from the day you learned of the decision (Administrative Appeals Act Article 27; Administrative Litigation Act Article 20)
steps.tip: You can also file a lawsuit directly without going through an administrative appeal (Administrative Litigation Act Article 18).

steps.title: Applying for a stay of execution
steps.desc: Within the departure deadline, we apply for a stay of execution together with the administrative appeal or lawsuit. We work backward from the deadline so that it does not pass before a decision is made.
steps.tip: A decision takes time, so filing just before the deadline may be too late.

steps.title: Organizing arguments and evidence
steps.desc: We organize your life during your stay, family relationships, employment and tax records, and the circumstances of any criminal record to show that the decision is excessively harsh.
steps.tip: Permission to change status of stay is discretionary, but a decision based on a factual error or that violates the principle of proportionality is unlawful (Supreme Court 2015Du48846).

steps.title: After the ruling or judgment
steps.desc: If the decision is cancelled, your case is reviewed again so you can obtain permission to stay. If your claim is dismissed, we decide together whether an appeal, reapplying or preparing to leave is the better option.

processes.summary: The departure deadline on the refusal notice sets how much time you have to challenge it. Here are the steps, from checking the notice to the stay of execution and what happens after the ruling or judgment.

areaPages.title: Refusal of Stay Extension or Change of Status
areaPages.lead: If your extension of stay or change of status of stay is refused, the notice will also state a departure deadline. To challenge the refusal, you must act before that deadline passes. Filing a lawsuit alone does not stop the departure deadline.

seo.title: Visa Extension Refused or Change of Status Refused in Korea | Jisan Law Foreigner Center
seo.description: If your visa extension or change of status was refused in Korea: checking the departure deadline, choosing between reapplying, an administrative appeal and an administrative lawsuit, applying for a stay of execution, and challenging abuse of discretion, explained from the applicant's point of view.

situations.title: When you should get advice
items: I applied to extend my stay and received a refusal notice (불허 통지서)
I tried to switch to a work visa after graduating, but the change was refused
The notice gives a date two weeks from now as my departure deadline
I was told my extension was refused because of a past fine
I was refused because the company's documents were incomplete, but the company will not help
My whole family is in Korea, and leaving would destroy our life here

items.name: Immigration Act Articles 24 and 25 (Permission to Change Status of Stay; Permission to Extend Period of Stay)
items.text: To engage in activities that fall under a different status of stay, you must first obtain permission to change your status of stay. To remain beyond your period of stay, you must obtain permission to extend it before the period ends.

items.name: Enforcement Decree of the Immigration Act Article 33 (Notice of Departure When Status of Stay Is Not Granted)
items.text: When an extension or change is not permitted, the applicant is notified, and the notice states a departure deadline no later than 14 days from its issue date. When a change is not permitted, the applicant may be allowed to keep staying under the status of stay already granted.

items.name: Administrative Litigation Act Article 20 (Filing Period) and Article 23 (Stay of Execution)
items.text: A lawsuit to cancel a decision must be filed within 90 days of the day you learned of the decision, and cannot be filed once 1 year has passed from the date of the decision. Filing a lawsuit does not suspend the decision, but if there is an urgent need to prevent harm that would be hard to undo, the court can order a stay of execution.

items.name: Administrative Appeals Act Article 27 (Period for Filing an Appeal)
items.text: An administrative appeal must be filed within 90 days of the day you learned of the decision and within 180 days of the date of the decision.

sections.title: Two things to check first on the notice
body: The refusal notice states the reason for refusal and the departure deadline. In principle, the departure deadline is set no later than 14 days from the notice's issue date. However, if the Ministry of Justice considers it necessary, it may set the expiry date of your already-permitted period of stay as the departure deadline.

When a change of status of stay is refused, you may sometimes be allowed to stay for the remaining period under the status you already hold. In that case, the notice may not state a departure deadline. First check which case applies to your notice.

The reason for refusal is often written in just one or two short lines. Ask the official in charge which requirement they found lacking, and write down the answer. This helps you decide the next step.

sections.title: Deciding whether to reapply or to challenge the decision
body: If you were refused because of missing documents, such as proof of income or company documents, it may be faster to add them and reapply. On the other hand, if the problem is a judgment call, such as a criminal record, doubts about the purpose of your stay or suspicion of false documents, reapplying is likely to lead to the same result.

According to Supreme Court precedent, even when the requirements are met, the authorities have discretion to decide whether to grant a change of status of stay by considering the applicant's eligibility, the purpose of the stay and the effect on the public interest. However, a decision based on a factual error, or one so excessive that it violates the principle of proportionality, goes beyond that discretion and is unlawful (Supreme Court Decision 2015Du48846, July 14, 2016). In an administrative appeal or lawsuit, this must be shown with evidence.

sections.title: Filing a lawsuit does not change the departure deadline
body: Filing an administrative appeal or an administrative lawsuit does not suspend the decision. If the departure deadline passes, you will be overstaying and may face deportation or punishment. That is why you must also apply for a stay of execution within the deadline and get a decision.

For a stay of execution, you must show harm that would be hard to undo and an urgent need. Prepare documents on circumstances that could not be reversed if you left, such as family living with you, study or medical treatment schedules, or ongoing court cases. A decision can take several days, so filing just before the departure deadline may be too late.
bullets: Mark both the departure deadline and the deadline for an appeal or lawsuit on your calendar.
If you cannot leave within the deadline because of illness or lack of transportation, you can separately apply to postpone the departure deadline (Enforcement Rules Article 33).
Once the deadline has passed, your options to challenge the decision become very limited.

sections.title: What is argued in an appeal or lawsuit
body: If the reason for refusal is factually wrong, we correct it with evidence. For example, if the reason is doubt about the purpose of your stay, we show your actual activities with work records, attendance records and salary transfer records.

Even if the reason itself is correct, you can argue that the decision is too harsh. We show whether the violation was minor, whether it happened long ago, whether you have lived responsibly since, and whether you have family and a life in Korea. If a criminal record is the problem, we submit the judgment together with evidence of compensation to the victim and settlement.

steps.title: How the Jisan Law Foreigner Center handles your case

items.title: Calculating the dates
items.desc: We check the notice's issue date, the date you received it, the departure deadline and your current expiry date, and first set the deadlines for the stay of execution and the appeal or lawsuit.

items.title: Analyzing the reason for refusal
items.desc: We review the notice together with your application documents, determine whether the issue is a requirement or a discretionary judgment, and then decide between reapplying and challenging the decision.

items.title: Filing the stay of execution and the appeal or complaint
items.desc: Within the departure deadline, we file the administrative appeal or the lawsuit and apply for a stay of execution at the same time.

items.title: Adding evidence and making arguments
items.desc: We organize your work, study, family and tax records and the circumstances of any criminal record, and argue that the decision is unlawful or excessive.

items.title: After the outcome
items.desc: If the decision is cancelled, we guide you through the new review. If your claim is dismissed, we decide together whether an appeal, reapplying or preparing to leave is the better option.

faqs.q: How many days after receiving the refusal notice do I have to file a lawsuit?
faqs.a: The legal deadline for a lawsuit is 90 days from the day you learned of the decision. However, the departure deadline on the notice comes much sooner. In practice, you need to file the lawsuit and the application for a stay of execution together within the departure deadline in order to remain in Korea while you challenge the decision.

faqs.q: Can I apply for an extension on the day my period of stay ends?
faqs.a: You must apply for an extension before your period of stay ends (Enforcement Decree of the Immigration Act Article 31(1)). If you apply after the expiry date, you will be overstaying, which can lead to an immigration fine or other disadvantages, so apply with time to spare.

faqs.q: Can I reapply and file an administrative lawsuit at the same time?
faqs.a: In some cases, yes. However, if you are refused again for the same reason, you only lose time, so it is better to first consider whether the reason for refusal can be fixed and then decide the order.

faqs.q: If I lose the administrative appeal, can I still file a lawsuit?
faqs.a: Even if your administrative appeal is dismissed, you can file an administrative lawsuit within 90 days of receiving the written ruling (재결서) (Administrative Litigation Act Article 20(1)). You can also go straight to a lawsuit from the start.

areaPages.areaName: Cancellation of Stay Permit or Permanent Residency
areaPages.title: Cancellation of Stay Permit or Permanent Residency
areaPages.lead: A stay permit or permanent residency you already hold can be cancelled if there are grounds set by law. If you receive a notice to appear and state your opinion, that is your chance to explain your circumstances before a decision is made.

seo.title: Stay Permit Cancellation and Permanent Residency (F-5) Cancellation in Korea | Jisan Law Foreigner Center
seo.description: When a stay permit or permanent residency in Korea is cancelled for false documents, breach of permit conditions or violations of law: preparing for the hearing, the grounds for cancelling permanent residency and applying for a general status of stay, and administrative appeals, lawsuits and stays of execution against the cancellation.

situations.title: When you should get advice
items: I received a notice from the immigration office to appear regarding the cancellation of my stay permit
I am being investigated because documents I submitted in the past are said to be untrue
After my criminal judgment became final, I was told my permanent residency may be cancelled
I was told that my guarantor has withdrawn their guarantee
I want to know whether I must leave right away if my permanent residency is cancelled

items.name: Immigration Act Article 89 (Cancellation or Change of Permits)
items.text: A visa, entry permit, stay permit or other permit can be cancelled or changed if the guarantor withdraws the guarantee or no longer exists, if it turns out the permit was obtained by false or improper means, if the permit conditions were breached, if circumstances have changed so seriously that the permit cannot be maintained, or if the violation of law is serious or a legitimate official order was violated. If necessary, the person is called to appear and give their opinion, and must be informed of the reasons, date, time and place at least 7 days before the hearing date.

items.name: Immigration Act Article 89-2 (Special Rules on Cancelling Permanent Residency)
items.text: Permanent residency can be cancelled only if it was obtained by false or improper means (must be cancelled), if a sentence of imprisonment with or without labor of 2 years or more becomes final for a crime under laws set by Ministry of Justice ordinance, if the total of prison sentences that became final within the last 5 years is 3 years or more, if the conditions of acquisition such as investment were breached, or if the person acted against the national interest. Even if it is cancelled, a general status of stay can be granted on application if the person needs to keep staying and meets the requirements.

items.name: Immigration Act Article 68(1)(3) and (3-2) (Departure Order)
items.text: A departure order can be issued to a person whose stay permit has been cancelled or whose permanent residency has been cancelled (except those granted a general status of stay).

sections.title: Cancellation is easiest to prevent before the decision
body: Cancellation of a stay permit usually starts with a request to appear or an investigation. The law provides that, if necessary, the foreigner is called to appear and give their opinion, and must be told the reasons for the intended cancellation, the date, time and place at least 7 days before the hearing. If you have received this notice, it means you still have a chance to explain your circumstances before a decision is made.

Before you appear, check each reason stated in the notice. You need to know which document or which action at what time is the problem in order to choose evidence to rebut it. If it is hard to explain in Korean, ask for an interpreter, and after giving your statement, ask for what was written to be read back to you.

sections.title: Common grounds for cancellation
body: The most common is suspicion that documents submitted with the application were untrue, such as sham employment, an address where you do not actually live, or a marriage that does not match the facts. The issue then becomes whether you intended to deceive from the start or whether your circumstances changed. Evidence showing the situation at the time the documents were prepared is important.

Permits are also cancelled on the ground that the violation of law was serious. A case in which you received a criminal penalty is a typical example. Even for the same offense, the assessment differs depending on how it happened, compensation to the victim and how you have lived since, so we do not just submit the judgment but also organize the circumstances surrounding the case.

sections.title: Permanent residency has its own grounds for cancellation
body: Permanent residency (F-5) has narrower grounds for cancellation than an ordinary stay permit. It can be cancelled only in the five cases set by law, and it must be cancelled if it was obtained by false or improper means. If a criminal case is the issue, you need to calculate whether the final sentence is 2 years or more, or whether the sentences that became final in the last 5 years add up to 3 years or more.

Even if your permanent residency is cancelled, you can receive a general status of stay on application if you need to keep staying in Korea and meet the requirements for a general status of stay. If this application is accepted, you are no longer subject to a departure order. Gather evidence in advance showing your family, job and long life in Korea.

sections.title: If you have received a cancellation decision
body: You can challenge a cancellation decision through an administrative appeal or administrative lawsuit. It must be filed within 90 days of the day you learned of the decision. A departure order is often issued together with the cancellation, so the first priority is applying for a stay of execution within the departure deadline.

In a lawsuit, we argue whether the grounds for cancellation actually existed and, even if they did, whether they were serious enough to justify cancellation. We use evidence to show your long life in Korea, any family members with Korean nationality, how the violation happened and your conduct since then.

steps.title: How the Jisan Law Foreigner Center handles your case

items.title: Checking the notice and the reasons
items.desc: We check the legal provisions and reasons stated in the notice to appear or the decision, and organize the documents and facts at issue in chronological order.

items.title: Preparing your statement
items.desc: Before the hearing, we organize what you will explain and the evidence to submit, and practice with likely questions. If needed, we also submit a written opinion.

items.title: Considering an application for a general status of stay
items.desc: If cancellation of permanent residency is expected, we check the requirements for a general status of stay and prepare the application documents.

items.title: Challenging the decision and stay of execution
items.desc: Once a decision is issued, we file an administrative appeal or administrative lawsuit, and if a departure order was also issued, we apply for a stay of execution.

faqs.q: What happens if I do not go after receiving a notice to appear?
faqs.a: You would be giving up your chance to appear and give your opinion, so the office is more likely to decide based only on the materials it has. If the date does not work for you, contact them in advance to ask for a different date, and if you cannot appear, at least submit your opinion in writing.

faqs.q: Will my permanent residency be cancelled if I receive a fine?
faqs.a: The grounds for cancelling permanent residency are based on sentences of imprisonment with or without labor, so a fine alone does not meet them (Immigration Act Article 89-2(1)). However, it may affect other grounds for cancellation or a later naturalization review, so it is still important to work to reduce the outcome.

faqs.q: I received both a cancellation decision and a departure order. Do I need to challenge both?
faqs.a: The two decisions are separate, so you need to check whether each one needs to be challenged. Usually, we argue that the cancellation is unlawful and at the same time ask for a stay of execution of the departure order.

faqs.q: Is my permit cancelled immediately if my guarantor withdraws their guarantee?
faqs.a: A guarantor withdrawing their guarantee or no longer existing can be a ground for cancellation, but cancellation is not mandatory (Immigration Act Article 89(1)(1)). Check whether you can find a new guarantor or whether you meet the requirements for stay without a guarantee, and submit your opinion.

items.name: Immigration Act Article 46 (Persons Subject to Deportation)
items.text: People who violated rules on entry, stay or employment, people who violated the duty of alien registration, people released after being sentenced to imprisonment without labor or a heavier sentence, and others can be deported. Permanent residents are deported only in exceptional cases, such as crimes of insurrection or foreign aggression, or people released after being sentenced to 5 years or more of imprisonment with or without labor who fall under Ministry of Justice ordinance.

items.name: Immigration Act Article 60 (Objection) and Article 61 (Special Permission to Stay)
items.text: An objection to a deportation order must be submitted to the Minister of Justice through the head of the regional immigration office within 7 days of receiving the order. Even if the objection is found to be without merit, the person may be permitted to stay if they previously held Korean nationality or have other special reasons to stay.

items.name: Immigration Act Articles 51, 52 and 55 (Detention, Detention Period, Request for Review)
items.text: If there are reasonable grounds to suspect a person is subject to deportation and there is a risk of flight, the person can be detained under a detention order. Detention for review and decision is limited to 10 days, which can be extended once by 10 days if unavoidable. The detained person or their legal representative or others may request a review of the detention by the Immigration Detention Committee.

items.name: Immigration Act Articles 63 and 65 (Detention of Persons Ordered to Be Deported; Temporary Release from Detention)
items.text: If the person cannot be removed immediately, they can be detained for up to 2 months. After that, detention can be extended by 3 months at a time with the approval of the Immigration Detention Committee, but not beyond a total of 9 months (20 months in exceptional cases). Detention can be temporarily lifted with conditions such as a deposit of KRW 20 million or less and restrictions on residence.

sections.title: First check which document you received
body: A departure recommendation (출국권고서), a departure order (출국명령서) and a deportation order (강제퇴거명령서) have similar names but different effects. A departure recommendation and a departure order tell you to leave on your own within a set deadline, while a deportation order is a decision under which the state removes you directly. If you leave after receiving a deportation order, you may be banned from entering for 5 years afterward, so the impact is much greater.

When the office hands you a deportation order, it must tell you that you can file an objection with the Minister of Justice. Be sure to write down the date you received it. The 7-day deadline for an objection is counted from that day.

sections.title: Objection and special permission to stay
body: The objection is submitted to the Minister of Justice through the head of the regional immigration office. It can include not only the argument that the grounds for deportation are factually wrong, but also the argument that even if they exist, you have special reasons to remain in Korea. Even if the Minister of Justice finds the objection without merit, the Minister can still permit you to stay.

Special reasons that are often used include a spouse or children with Korean nationality, a long life in Korea, an illness under treatment, ongoing court cases or wages still owed to you. Claims alone are not enough. You need verifiable evidence such as family relationship documents, medical certificates and court documents.

Separately from the objection, you can file an administrative lawsuit within 90 days of the day you learned of the decision. If removal is imminent, you must also apply for a stay of execution so that you are not removed while the lawsuit is pending.

sections.title: Immigration detention has time limits and procedures
body: Detention to review whether a person should be deported is limited to 10 days, and can be extended once by another 10 days if unavoidable. In the case of emergency detention, a detention order must be obtained within 48 hours, or the person must be released immediately. When someone is detained, their family, lawyer or others must be informed in writing within 3 days of the date, place and reason for detention.

If, after a deportation order, the person cannot be removed immediately because they have no passport or transportation, they can be detained for up to 2 months. Under the 2025 amendment, any extension after that requires the approval of the Immigration Detention Committee and can only be made 3 months at a time, and the total detention period in principle cannot exceed 9 months. Once the limit is exceeded, the person must be released immediately.

If you object to the detention itself, you can request a review by the Immigration Detention Committee. The Committee decides within 3 weeks of receiving the request, and can extend this once by up to 2 weeks if unavoidable (Enforcement Decree Article 70).

sections.title: Applying for temporary release from detention
body: The detained person, a guarantor, or a legal representative or others can apply to the Immigration Detention Committee for temporary release from detention. If release is granted, the person must deposit up to KRW 20 million and follow conditions such as restrictions on residence, regular reporting and naming a guarantor.

Attach evidence to the application explaining why release is needed and showing that the deposit can be paid. Giving specific reasons, such as medical treatment, a pending unpaid wage case or lawsuit, or caring for family, together with a place to stay and a guarantor, helps the decision. If the conditions are broken or an order to appear is ignored, the temporary release can be cancelled and the deposit may be forfeited to the state.

steps.title: How the Jisan Law Foreigner Center responds

items.title: Checking the place of detention and the documents
items.desc: Using the detention notice sent to the family or the order the person received, we confirm the place of detention, the type of decision and the date it was received.

items.title: Visiting and organizing the facts
items.desc: We visit the detention facility to hear the person's circumstances, and list the evidence to use in the objection and lawsuit. If needed, we arrange an interpreter.

items.title: Filing the objection and review request
items.desc: Within the 7-day deadline, we file the objection to the deportation order, and at the same time request a review of the detention or apply for temporary release.

items.title: Administrative lawsuit and stay of execution
items.desc: Separately from the objection, we file a lawsuit to cancel the decision and apply for a stay of execution to prevent removal and secure time to challenge it.

items.title: Settling remaining matters
items.desc: If removal cannot be avoided, we settle unpaid wages, deposits and pending cases before departure, and continue handling them as your representative.

faqs.q: Is there nothing I can do after 7 days?
faqs.a: An objection to the Minister of Justice cannot be filed after 7 days. However, an administrative lawsuit can be filed within 90 days of the day you learned of the decision, so quickly consider a lawsuit and a stay of execution before removal.

faqs.q: Can I visit my family member in the detention center?
faqs.a: Each detention facility has its own visiting procedures and hours. Visits by a lawyer are handled separately from ordinary visits. The family should first contact the detention facility to check how to visit, and get advice if they need to hire a lawyer.

faqs.q: If I pay the deposit, will I definitely be released?
faqs.a: No. Temporary release from detention is decided by looking at the detained person's circumstances, the reasons release is needed, their assets and so on. The deposit is money paid as a condition after release has been granted (Immigration Act Article 65). The first step is to show the reasons for release with evidence.

faqs.q: If I apply for refugee status, will I not be removed?
faqs.a: Under the Refugee Act, if you have applied for refugee recognition and no decision has been made, or the review of your objection has not ended, in principle you must not be removed (Immigration Act Article 62(4)). However, there are exceptions if there is a risk to public safety, and the reason the application was delayed can affect decisions about the detention period.

areaPages.title: Entry Ban and Visa Refusal
areaPages.lead: If a family member abroad is refused a visa (사증) or is stopped from entering at the airport, the first step is to find out why. Court precedent indicates that it is difficult for the foreign national themselves to challenge a visa refusal in court, so what you add when reapplying matters.

seo.title: Checking Entry Ban Reasons and Responding to Visa Refusal in Korea | Jisan Law Foreigner Center
seo.description: Marriage visa refusals, being refused entry at the airport, how to check the reason for an entry ban and prepare a reapplication, why a visa refusal is hard to challenge in court (Supreme Court 2014Du42506), and issues when a refusal is made without a written decision.

situations.title: When you should get advice
items: My foreign spouse's marriage migrant (F-6) visa was refused
I want to come back to Korea, but I was told I am subject to an entry ban
I was not allowed to enter at the airport and had to go back
I was deported in the past, but now I am married to a Korean
My visa was refused, but I did not receive the reasons in writing

items.name: Immigration Act Articles 7 and 8 (Entry of Foreigners; Visas)
items.text: Foreigners must enter with a valid passport and a visa issued by the Minister of Justice. People covered by visa waiver agreements and others are exceptions. The standards and procedures for issuing visas are set by Ministry of Justice ordinance.

items.name: Immigration Act Article 11 (Prohibition of Entry, etc.)
items.text: Entry can be prohibited for people who may pose a public health risk, people who may harm the interests or public safety of the Republic of Korea, or the economic order, social order or good morals, and people who left after receiving a deportation order less than 5 years ago, among others.

sections.title: An entry ban and a visa refusal are different problems
body: An entry ban is a decision by the Ministry of Justice to block a specific foreigner from entering, while a visa refusal means that a Korean embassy or consulate or the immigration office does not accept a visa application. If you are under an entry ban, a visa application is likely to be refused. You first need to tell whether the refusal was because of an entry ban or because of documents or requirements.

The most common reasons for an entry ban are past overstaying, illegal employment, deportation and criminal penalties. A person who left after receiving a deportation order may be banned from entering until 5 years have passed, and the actual length of the restriction depends on the reason.

sections.title: Why it is hard to challenge a visa refusal in court
body: In a lawsuit filed by a foreigner who was refused a marriage migrant (F-6) visa, the Supreme Court held that a foreigner does not have a legal interest in seeking cancellation of a visa refusal (Supreme Court Decision 2014Du42506, May 15, 2018). It cited the nature of visa issuance, the purpose of the Immigration Act and the principle of reciprocity, among other reasons.

On the other hand, in a case involving the refusal of an overseas Korean visa, the Supreme Court held that notifying the refusal only by phone without a written decision violated the Administrative Procedures Act, and that a refusal made without weighing the interests involved was a deviation from or abuse of discretion (Supreme Court Decision 2017Du38874, July 11, 2019). The same judgment found that an entry ban decision entered only into an internal computer system without being communicated externally was not a decision that could be challenged in court. Which options are open depends on the applicant's status and connection to Korea.

sections.title: What to add when reapplying
body: If a marriage migrant visa was refused, we check which requirement was found lacking, such as the genuineness of the marriage, the ability to communicate, or the inviting spouse's income and housing. Adding records of conversations and photos showing how the relationship developed, visit records and proof of income can sometimes change the result.

If the refusal is due to a past violation, we prepare evidence explaining the circumstances at the time, how much time has passed since then and your family relationships in Korea. Reapplying with the same documents without knowing the exact reason for refusal is likely to lead to the same result.

sections.title: If you were refused entry at the airport
body: At immigration inspection, officers check whether your passport and visa are valid, whether your purpose of entry fits your status of stay, and whether you are subject to an entry ban. If you cannot prove that you meet these requirements, you may not be permitted to enter (Immigration Act Article 12).

A person who is not permitted to enter can be temporarily held in the airport's holding room for foreigners for up to 48 hours, which can be extended once by another 48 hours if unavoidable (Article 56). It is difficult to change the decision within this short time. It is more realistic to find out the reason for refusal after you return and prepare for your next entry. If a company or family member is inviting you, have their documents ready in advance.

steps.title: How the Jisan Law Foreigner Center handles your case

items.title: Finding out how the refusal happened
items.desc: We check the refusal notice or the information given, as well as past immigration records, to determine whether it was due to an entry ban or a problem with requirements.

items.title: Deciding whether it can be challenged
items.desc: Looking at the applicant's status and how the decision was made (such as whether a written decision was given), we decide whether an administrative lawsuit is possible or whether reapplying is better.

items.title: Strengthening the reapplication
items.desc: We help you reapply by organizing evidence and a written explanation to meet the requirements found lacking.

items.title: Procedures for family in Korea
items.desc: We also prepare the documents and statements needed from your spouse or the inviting person in Korea.

faqs.q: Can I find out in advance whether I am subject to an entry ban?
faqs.a: In many cases, the person concerned checks whether there is an entry ban and how long it lasts by contacting the immigration office directly. Whether this can be checked through a representative depends on the office's guidance, so decide how to check it together during your consultation.

faqs.q: Can I ask for an entry ban to be lifted before it ends?
faqs.a: Where there are humanitarian reasons, such as living with Korean family members, people sometimes ask for the ban to be lifted. Whether to accept is at the Ministry of Justice's discretion, so the request must be backed with enough evidence of your circumstances.

faqs.q: Can my Korean spouse file a lawsuit on my behalf?
faqs.a: Court precedent held that the foreigner who applied for the visa has no legal interest in seeking its cancellation. Whether a Korean spouse can file a lawsuit directly depends on the content of the decision and which of the spouse's interests are affected, so we decide after looking at the decision and how it was made.

faqs.q: Can I call a lawyer at the airport after being refused entry?
faqs.a: You can contact one, but the temporary holding period is short, up to 48 hours, so it is difficult to change the decision within that time. It is more realistic to get help finding out the reason for refusal after you return and preparing to come back.

areaPages.areaName: Immigration Violation Review and Illegal Employment
areaPages.title: Immigration Violation Review and Illegal Employment
areaPages.lead: If you overstayed, worked without permission, or hired a foreigner who is not allowed to work, you will be investigated and reviewed by the immigration office. The outcome of this review decides whether you receive a notice to pay an immigration fine (범칙금 통고처분), a departure order, a deportation order or a criminal referral, so you need to prepare before you appear.

seo.title: Immigration Violation Review, Immigration Fine Notices and Illegal Employment Penalties in Korea | Jisan Law Foreigner Center
seo.description: For foreigners under immigration violation review for overstaying, activities outside their status of stay or changing workplaces without permission, and companies investigated for illegal employment: questioning and statement records, the 15-day deadline for immigration fine notices, criminal referral, the link to departure and deportation orders, and the 3-year hiring restriction.
keywords: illegal employment of foreigners penalty Korea

situations.title: When you should get advice
items: I did not realize my period of stay had expired, and the immigration office contacted me to appear
I am a D-2 student, and working more hours than permitted has become a problem
I changed companies without getting permission to change my workplace
I received a notice to pay an immigration fine and do not know whether to pay or challenge it
An immigration raid at our factory caught several foreign employees
A foreign worker we got through a staffing agency turned out not to have work authorization

items.name: Immigration Act Articles 47 and 48 (Investigation; Request to Appear and Questioning of Suspects)
items.text: Immigration officers can investigate foreigners suspected of being subject to deportation and, if necessary, request them to appear for questioning. Statements are recorded in a statement record, which must be read to the suspect or shown to them, and they must be asked whether anything needs correcting. The statements of a person who does not understand Korean must be interpreted by an interpreter.

items.name: Immigration Act Articles 101, 102 and 105 (Criminal Referral; Notice of Fine; Failure to Pay and Referral)
items.text: Immigration violation cases cannot be prosecuted without a criminal referral from the head of the immigration office. If an investigation confirms an offense, the head of the office can issue a notice to pay an immigration fine, and must refer the case immediately if it appears to warrant imprisonment without labor or a heavier sentence. If the fine is not paid within 15 days of receiving the notice, the case must be referred, but not if a deportation order has been issued.

items.name: Immigration Act Articles 94 and 95 (Penalties)
items.text: People who overstayed, engaged in other activities without permission for activities outside their status of stay, or hired people without a work-eligible status of stay, among others, face imprisonment of up to 3 years or a fine of up to KRW 30 million. People who changed workplaces without permission or hired such foreigners, or violated the duty of alien registration, among others, face imprisonment of up to 1 year or a fine of up to KRW 10 million.

items.name: Immigration Act Article 99-3; Act on the Employment of Foreign Workers Article 20
items.text: Illegal employment and hiring foreigners without permission to change workplace are subject to joint penalty provisions (양벌규정), so the corporation or business owner can also be fined. An employer punished for violating the Immigration Act or similar laws can be restricted from hiring foreign workers for 3 years from the date of the violation.

sections.title: What is an immigration violation review?
body: An immigration offender (출입국사범) is a person found to have violated the penalty provisions of the Immigration Act. Common examples on the foreigner's side are overstaying, working or changing workplaces without permission, and failing to meet the alien registration duty. Companies and their representatives who hire foreigners not allowed to work are also immigration offenders.

These cases are investigated by the immigration office, not the police. Even if the police learn of a case first, they must hand it over to the office, and it cannot be prosecuted without a referral from the head of the office (Article 101). So the office's investigation and review effectively decide the direction of the case.

sections.title: What to keep in mind during questioning
body: If needed for the investigation, the office will ask you to appear for questioning and record your statement in a statement record. The record must be read to you or shown to you, and you must be asked whether anything was written incorrectly. If you ask for additions or changes, those must also be recorded. If your Korean is limited, ask for an interpreter.

It is important to explain truthfully how the violation happened. If there were circumstances such as your company not giving you the extension documents, missing the deadline because you were hospitalized, or being misinformed about the procedure to change workplaces, bring messages, medical certificates or documents that show this.

sections.title: The review can lead to several outcomes
body: If a violation is confirmed, the case may end with a notice to pay an immigration fine, you may receive a departure order after the notice (Article 68(1)(5)), or, if the violation is serious, it may lead to a deportation order or a criminal referral. If the case appears to warrant imprisonment without labor or a heavier sentence, the head of the office must refer it immediately.

If you pay the immigration fine, the case does not go to criminal trial, but the violation record may be considered in later reviews for extension of stay or change of status of stay. When you receive a notice to pay an immigration fine, you must decide within 15 days whether to pay or dispute the violation.

sections.title: When a company is investigated
body: Hiring a person without a work-eligible status of stay is punishable by imprisonment of up to 3 years or a fine of up to KRW 30 million, and hiring a foreigner who has not obtained permission to change workplace is punishable by imprisonment of up to 1 year or a fine of up to KRW 10 million. A corporation can also be fined under the joint penalty provisions, but can avoid this if it exercised considerable care and supervision to prevent the violation (Article 99-3).

In the investigation, what matters is whether you knew the worker's status of stay, whether you checked their residence card, and how many people you hired for how long. If you are punished, you may be restricted from hiring foreign workers for 3 years, which can be a bigger burden than the fine itself. Organize your hiring documents, verification records and staffing agency contracts before giving your statement.

sections.title: Duties companies must follow at all times
body: Before hiring, check the worker's status of stay, period of stay and permitted scope of activities using their residence card, and keep a record. In some cases, such as student (D-2) or job seeker (D-10) status, the person needs permission for activities outside their status of stay to work.

If a foreign employee is dismissed, resigns, dies or cannot be reached, or if important terms of the employment contract change, you must report it to the office within 15 days. Failing to do so can lead to an administrative fine (과태료) of up to KRW 2 million (Articles 19 and 100). You must not discriminate against workers because they are foreign, and if you provide a dormitory, you must give information such as its structure, location and size before signing the contract.

steps.title: How the Jisan Law Foreigner Center handles your case

items.title: Checking the violation and your stay situation
items.desc: We look at the request to appear or the notice and your stay records to first check which provision is at issue and how it may affect your stay.

items.title: Organizing the facts and preparing for questioning
items.desc: We organize how the violation happened in date order, gather supporting evidence, and practice with likely questions.

items.title: Responding to fine notices and departure measures
items.desc: We decide whether to pay the fine or dispute it, and if it leads to a departure order or deportation proceedings, we handle statements of opinion, objections and administrative lawsuits.

items.title: Company response and advice
items.desc: We prepare statements for companies that were raided and challenge hiring restrictions or cancellations of employment permits. The same lawyer then continues to review your hiring procedures and reporting duties.

faqs.q: If I pay the immigration fine, is there no problem with my stay?
faqs.a: If you pay the immigration fine, the case does not go to criminal trial, but if the head of the office considers departure measures appropriate after the notice, a departure order can be issued (Immigration Act Article 68(1)(5)). Even if you can continue staying, the violation record may be considered in your next review.

faqs.q: What happens if I cannot pay the immigration fine on time?
faqs.a: If you do not pay within 15 days of receiving the notice, the head of the office must refer the case for prosecution, and criminal proceedings begin (Article 105). If you pay before the referral, the case will not be referred. If it is hard to pay within the deadline, contact the office in advance.

faqs.q: If the company did not know the worker's status of stay, will it avoid punishment?
faqs.a: The company can argue that it had no intent, but this is more likely to be accepted if it can show with records what checks it made. Keeping records of checking residence cards and hiring documents is the most reliable preparation.

faqs.q: What about the unpaid wages of employees caught in a raid?
faqs.a: Pay for work done must be paid regardless of status of stay. Settling wages and severance pay before the employee is detained or leaves reduces disputes later.

areaPages.areaName: Refusal of Naturalization or Permanent Residency (F-5)
areaPages.title: Refusal of Naturalization or Permanent Residency (F-5)
areaPages.lead: If your application for naturalization or permanent residency is refused, the first step is to find out exactly which requirement was the problem. If it is something that cannot be changed, such as a past fine, the key is how to show how it happened and how you have lived since.

seo.title: Naturalization Refused or Permanent Residency (F-5) Refused in Korea: Response and Lawsuits | Jisan Law Foreigner Center
seo.description: Requirements for general and simplified naturalization in Korea, how past fines and immigration fines affect the good conduct requirement, permanent residency requirements, and whether to reapply or file an administrative lawsuit after a refusal, explained from the applicant's point of view.

situations.title: When you should get advice
items: My naturalization application was refused for lack of good conduct
I was told I cannot naturalize because of a drunk driving fine from a few years ago
I applied for simplified naturalization through marriage, but was refused because we are separated
I applied to change to permanent residency, but was told I do not meet the income requirement
I failed the naturalization interview and do not know when I can apply again

items.name: Nationality Act Article 5 (Requirements for General Naturalization)
items.text: The requirements are having had an address in Korea continuously for 5 years or more, holding a status of stay that allows permanent residence, being an adult, good conduct including compliance with laws, the ability to support yourself, Korean language ability and basic knowledge, and not harming national security and similar interests.

items.name: Nationality Act Article 6(2) (Requirements for Simplified Naturalization: Spouses of Korean Nationals)
items.text: A person who has had an address in Korea continuously for 2 years or more while married to a Korean national, or who has had an address in Korea for 1 year or more while married after 3 years have passed since the marriage, among others, can be granted naturalization without the 5-year residence and permanent residence status requirements. A person who could not continue married life for reasons they were not responsible for, such as the spouse's death or disappearance, can also be granted naturalization after completing the remaining period, if the Minister of Justice finds it appropriate.

items.name: Enforcement Decree of the Immigration Act, Appended Table 1-3 (Persons Eligible for Permanent Residency)
items.text: Permanent residency is granted to people who do not fall under the grounds for deportation and who meet the requirements of each item, for example, the spouse or minor child of a Korean national or permanent resident who has stayed for 2 years or more, or an adult who has stayed for 5 years or more under certain statuses of stay.

sections.title: We find out the specific reason for refusal
body: Naturalization and permanent residency are granted after reviewing whether the requirements are met, so the response depends on which requirement is stated in the refusal notice. For requirements calculated by dates, such as the period of residence or status of stay, it is clear when you can reapply. For requirements involving an assessment, such as good conduct or the ability to support yourself, you must make your case with evidence.
If the reason in the notice is brief, ask the office which specific facts it relied on. You can also check the review materials through an information disclosure request (정보공개청구).

sections.title: Past fines and the good conduct requirement
body: In practice, the requirement that causes the most problems is good conduct. If you have a record such as a fine, an immigration fine or a suspended indictment, when it happened, what it was for and what outcome you received are all reviewed. The law leaves the specific standards to Ministry of Justice ordinance, so decisions vary from case to case.

You cannot change an outcome you have already received, but you can show how it happened, compensation to the victim, and a record of law-abiding life in the years since. If you are thinking about naturalization, you should also consider that the outcome of a criminal case currently in progress may affect your naturalization timeline.

sections.title: Simplified naturalization for married applicants and separation
body: The spouse of a Korean national can apply for simplified naturalization after having an address in Korea for 2 years or more while married. If you separate or a divorce lawsuit begins during the review, the requirement of being married may become a problem.

If you could not continue married life because of the spouse's death or disappearance or other reasons you were not responsible for, there is a way to be granted naturalization after completing the remaining period. If the marriage broke down because of the spouse's violence or leaving home, gather evidence showing this.

sections.title: Reapply or file a lawsuit?
body: If the missing requirement can be met with time, reapplying is the realistic option. If there are grounds to believe the facts were misunderstood or that you were treated differently from others in the same situation, you can file an administrative lawsuit within 90 days of the day you learned of the decision.
Naturalization is an area where the authorities are given broad discretion, so in a lawsuit you must specifically show that the facts on which the decision was based were wrong.

sections.title: If your change to permanent residency was refused
body: Permanent residency (F-5) is usually applied for by changing from your current status of stay. If the change of status is refused, you may be allowed to stay for the remaining period under the status you already hold (Enforcement Decree of the Immigration Act Article 33(1)). So if the notice does not state a departure deadline, you can plan your next steps based on the expiry date of your current status.

If the requirement can be met with time, such as income or length of stay, it is common to reapply at that point. If a criminal record or conduct was the problem, build up a record of your life and prepare a written explanation before your next application.

steps.title: How the Jisan Law Foreigner Center handles your case

items.title: Checking each requirement
items.desc: We calculate each requirement one by one, such as period of residence, status of stay, income and past records, and compare them with the reason for refusal.

items.title: Organizing records of past incidents
items.desc: We gather the decisions on fines or immigration fines, how they happened, compensation to the victim and records of your life since, and prepare explanatory materials.

items.title: Deciding the direction
items.desc: We decide whether to calculate the timing for reapplication or to challenge the decision in an administrative lawsuit.

items.title: Written submissions and litigation
items.desc: We write the opinion for reapplication or the complaint, and if it goes to court, we handle the hearings as well.

faqs.q: I received a fine for drunk driving. Can I never naturalize?
faqs.a: It is not permanent, but it will be counted against you in the good conduct review, and in many cases you can only be assessed again after a certain period has passed. The specific time standards depend on Ministry of Justice ordinance and internal standards, so they need to be calculated based on the date and content of the decision.

faqs.q: Can a naturalization refusal be challenged through an administrative appeal?
faqs.a: A naturalization refusal is also a decision of the Minister of Justice, so it can be challenged through an administrative appeal or administrative lawsuit. Both must be filed within 90 days of the day you learned of the decision.

faqs.q: What if a criminal case arises while my permanent residency application is under review?
faqs.a: Even during the review, a new case can affect the result. Work to reduce the outcome of the criminal case, and get advice on how to handle your application before a decision is made in that case.

seo.description: When your Korean spouse will not cooperate with your visa extension, staying during separation or a divorce lawsuit, special extension rules for domestic violence victims, and the main responsibility for the breakdown of the marriage under F-6 item (c) (Supreme Court 2018Du66869), explained from the marriage migrant's point of view.

situations.title: When you should get advice
items: My husband says he will not sign or stamp my visa extension documents
I left home because of my spouse's violence and am staying at a shelter
My Korean spouse filed for divorce, and I am worried I will have to leave Korea if we divorce
My spouse suddenly passed away, and I do not know how to continue my stay
I am raising the child I gave birth to in Korea on my own
Immigration says they will carry out an on-site investigation (실태조사) to check whether our marriage is genuine

items.name: Enforcement Decree of the Immigration Act, Appended Table 1-2 (Marriage Migrant F-6)
items.text: It covers (a) (가목) the spouse of a Korean national; (b) (나목) a father or mother raising a child born from a marriage (including a de facto marriage) with a Korean national; and (c) (다목) a person who was staying in Korea while married to a Korean spouse and cannot maintain a normal marriage because of the spouse's death or disappearance or other reasons they are not responsible for.

items.name: Immigration Act Article 25-2 (Special Rules for Marriage Migrants, etc.)
items.text: If the spouse of a Korean national or a similar person who has a trial, investigation or other legal remedy in progress because of domestic violence applies to extend their period of stay, the extension can be permitted until the procedure ends, and further extended afterward if needed for recovery from the harm.

items.name: Act on Private International Law Article 66 (Divorce)
items.text: If one of the spouses is a Korean national whose habitual residence is in Korea, the divorce is governed by Korean law.

sections.title: Your status of stay is tied to your marital status
body: Marriage migrant (F-6) item (a) is a status of stay based on being the spouse of a Korean national. So at every extension review, the authorities check whether the marriage is actually being maintained. That is why the review becomes difficult if you do not live together or your spouse does not cooperate.

That does not mean you must leave whenever the marriage breaks down. If you are raising a child born from a marriage with a Korean national, you can continue your stay under item (b). If the marriage cannot be maintained because of the spouse's death or disappearance or other reasons you are not responsible for, you can continue under item (c).

sections.title: The key is who is mainly responsible
body: The Supreme Court interprets 'reasons they are not responsible for' in item (c) as cases where the Korean spouse is mainly responsible for the breakdown of the marriage. It does not mean the foreign spouse must be completely without fault. The Court also held that in a lawsuit challenging a refusal of status of stay, the burden of proving that reason lies with the authorities, and that the family court's findings in the divorce judgment should in principle be respected (Supreme Court Decision 2018Du66869, July 4, 2019).

That is why how the divorce is handled is directly tied to your stay. If you rush to finish with a divorce by agreement (협의이혼), there is no record of who was responsible. If there are circumstances such as the spouse's violence, leaving home, failure to pay living expenses or an affair, making that responsibility clear in a judicial divorce (재판상 이혼) may help in the immigration review.

sections.title: If you have suffered domestic violence
body: A marriage migrant who has an investigation, trial or protection procedure in progress because of domestic violence can receive extensions of stay until the procedure ends. Even after the procedure ends, the stay can be extended if needed for recovery from the harm.

If there was violence, collect police report records, medical certificates, photos of injuries and confirmation of use of a counseling center or shelter. These materials are used in the criminal proceedings, the divorce lawsuit and the immigration review. If you are worried about being reported to immigration when you are questioned as a victim, discuss that in your consultation as well.

sections.title: Preparing for on-site investigations and extension reviews
body: The immigration office sometimes carries out on-site investigations to check whether a marriage is genuine or how it broke down. What you tell the investigator is recorded and later used in reviews and lawsuits, so it is important not to say anything untrue or answer with guesses.

If you are separated, write down why and when the separation began, and keep records of who paid living expenses and how you kept in contact. The outcome of an extension during a divorce lawsuit depends on the office's judgment, so it is a good idea to apply early with the lawsuit documents ready.

steps.title: How the Jisan Law Foreigner Center handles your case

items.title: Reviewing your stay and marriage together
items.desc: We check your expiry date, whether you have children, how the separation happened and whether there was violence, and see which path is possible under F-6 items (a), (b) or (c).

items.title: Organizing evidence
items.desc: We organize conversation records, police reports, medical certificates and money transfer records that show responsibility for the breakdown of the marriage.

items.title: Divorce lawsuit and stay application in parallel
items.desc: While arguing over responsibility in the judicial divorce, we also prepare the documents for an extension of stay or change of status.

items.title: Challenging a refusal
items.desc: If your stay is refused, we bring an administrative appeal or administrative lawsuit based on the findings of the divorce judgment.

faqs.q: If my husband does not cooperate with my extension, will it be refused?
faqs.a: It is true that the review becomes difficult without your spouse's cooperation. However, if the reason they will not cooperate is that the marriage has broken down, other paths such as item (c) or the special rules for domestic violence can be considered. Keep messages and other records showing their refusal to cooperate.

faqs.q: Is a divorce by agreement bad for my stay?
faqs.a: A divorce by agreement is not bad in itself, but there will be no record of whose responsibility the breakdown was. To obtain F-6 item (c), you must show with other evidence that the Korean spouse was mainly responsible, so get advice before deciding how to divorce.

faqs.q: If I am raising a child, can I keep living in Korea after the divorce?
faqs.a: A parent raising a child born from a marriage with a Korean national can obtain marriage migrant (F-6) item (b) status. Custody and actually raising the child are important, so in the divorce lawsuit you should also argue over who will be designated as the person with parental authority and the custodial parent.

faqs.q: My Korean spouse suddenly passed away. Can I continue my stay?
faqs.a: The spouse's death is a reason expressly listed in marriage migrant (F-6) item (c). Prepare family relationship documents and documents related to the death showing that you were staying in Korea while married, and proceed with the immigration procedures. Since inheritance issues also arise, check the deadline (3 months) for renouncing the inheritance (상속포기) or accepting it with limited liability (한정승인).

areaPages.areaName: Questioning and Arrest of Foreign Suspects
areaPages.title: Questioning and Arrest of Foreign Suspects
areaPages.lead: Foreigners are investigated under the same procedures as Koreans, but with additional rights such as interpretation and consular notification. The most important thing is to make sure you understand exactly what is in the statement record written in Korean before you sign it.

seo.title: Police Questioning of Foreigners in Korea: Interpreters, Consular Notification on Arrest and Lawyer Visits | Jisan Law Foreigner Center
seo.description: The legal basis for foreign suspects to request an interpreter during police questioning in Korea, how to check the statement record again through the interpreter, consular notification and visits upon arrest or detention, translated warrants, family requests for a lawyer to attend, and the new Public Prosecution Service system from October 2026.

situations.title: When you should get advice
items: I received a text from the police asking me to appear as a suspect, but my Korean is poor
My husband was arrested, and I do not know whether to inform the embassy
During questioning, the interpreter seemed to shorten what I said
I signed a statement record in Korean without knowing what it said
I was told that an arrest warrant (구속영장) has been requested
My departure date is approaching, but the investigation has not finished

items.name: Police Investigation Rules Article 91 (Questioning of Foreigners)
items.text: When questioning a foreigner, judicial police officers must provide interpretation in a language the person understands. When arresting or detaining a foreigner, they must inform the person that they can freely meet and communicate with consular officers and can request that the consulate be notified of the arrest or detention, and if requested, must notify the consulate without delay.

items.name: Criminal Procedure Act Article 180 (Interpretation) and Article 244 (Preparation of the Suspect Interrogation Record)
items.text: The statements of a person who does not understand Korean must be interpreted by an interpreter. The record must be shown or read to the suspect, and if the suspect raises an objection, it must be added to the record.

items.name: Criminal Procedure Act Article 243-2 (Participation of Defense Counsel, etc.)
items.text: If requested by the suspect or their defense counsel, legal representative, spouse, lineal relatives or siblings, the judicial police officer must allow defense counsel to meet the suspect or attend the questioning.

items.name: Rules on Criminal Investigation Articles 215, 217 and 218
items.text: In questioning, arresting or detaining foreigners, their language, customs and habits must be considered, and if a treaty requires the consulate to be notified regardless of the person's wishes, the consulate must be notified. If the person is not fluent in Korean, the record must be prepared through an interpreter, and a translation must be attached when executing a warrant or providing a list of seized items.

sections.title: Interpretation is a right you can request
body: When the police question a foreigner, they must provide interpretation in a language the person understands. If you are questioned without an interpreter because you can manage everyday conversation, your meaning can easily be misunderstood in questions about intent or how the incident happened. Before you appear, clearly tell the investigator that you need an interpreter and in which language.

It is better to avoid having a family member or friend interpret. Interpretation by someone with an interest in the case may later be considered unreliable. Instead, if you need emotional support because of your nationality or other reasons, you can ask for a person you trust to sit with you (Criminal Procedure Act Article 244-5).

sections.title: Check the statement record again through the interpreter before signing
body: The statement record is written in Korean. Ask the interpreter to read the record back to you from the beginning, and ask for anything that differs from what you said to be corrected. If you raise an objection, it must be added to the record, and the original sentences before correction must remain readable.

The police must record that the statement record was read to you through an interpreter and obtain the interpreter's signature (Rules on Criminal Investigation Article 40). Signing without understanding is the most dangerous thing. If you are tired or do not understand, ask for a break.

sections.title: If you are arrested, you can have your consulate informed
body: When a foreigner is arrested or detained, the police must tell them that they can meet and communicate with consular officers and can ask for the consulate to be informed of the arrest or detention. This right also comes from Article 36 of the Vienna Convention on Consular Relations. If you request it, the police must notify the consulate without delay, and for some countries, the consulate is notified under a treaty regardless of the person's wishes.

A translation must be attached when a warrant is executed and when a list of seized items is given. If an arrest warrant (구속영장) is not requested within 48 hours of the arrest, the person must be released. If a warrant is requested, a judge questions the person directly. If the person has no defense counsel at this hearing, a court-appointed defense counsel (국선변호인) is assigned.

sections.title: The new investigation structure from October 2026
body: From October 2, 2026, the Prosecutors' Office (검찰청) is abolished, and the Public Prosecution Service (공소청) handles indictments. Investigations are carried out by the police and the Serious Crimes Investigation Agency (중대범죄수사청), while prosecutors decide based on the case files and request supplementary investigation if needed. As a result, the statements made and materials submitted at the police stage may carry more weight.

Foreigners may be banned from leaving Korea while an investigation or trial is ongoing. If you have plans to leave, tell the investigator in advance and arrange the questioning schedule. If you received a notice of an exit ban (출국정지), you can file an objection within 10 days of receiving it or learning of it (Immigration Act Articles 29 and 4-5).

steps.title: How the Jisan Law Foreigner Center responds

items.title: Direct consultation
items.desc: A managing partner personally hears your case and also checks your status of stay, its expiry date and your departure plans. Consultations are available in English and Chinese.

items.title: Practicing for questioning
items.desc: We pick out likely questions and practice as if it were the real questioning. We also point out in advance how your words can change through interpretation.

items.title: Sitting in on questioning
items.desc: We go into the interview room with you, check that the interpreted questions and answers match what is written in the record, and object on the spot to leading or improper questions.

items.title: Visits after arrest and the pre-detention hearing
items.desc: We visit the arrested person, make sure consular notification and access to counsel are provided, and attend the pre-detention hearing (영장실질심사) to explain, with evidence of housing and ties to Korea, that detention is not necessary.

items.title: Written opinions and preparing for your stay
items.desc: We submit defense counsel's written opinions to the police and prosecutor, and also prepare for how the outcome will affect your stay.

faqs.q: Do I have to pay for the interpreter?
faqs.a: We have not found any rule requiring the suspect to pay for an interpreter appointed by the investigating agency for questioning. The situation is different if you use a separate interpreter for meetings with your lawyer or consultations, so check in advance.

faqs.q: I am worried that informing the consulate will leave a record in my home country.
faqs.a: In principle, consular notification is made when you request it. However, with some countries, a treaty may require notification regardless of your wishes. Whether you need consular assistance depends on the case and your nationality, so decide together during your consultation.

faqs.q: Can foreigners get a court-appointed defense counsel?
faqs.a: The same standards apply regardless of nationality. If you have no defense counsel at the arrest warrant hearing, the judge appoints one, and after indictment, the court appoints one depending on factors such as whether you are detained and the statutory penalty (Criminal Procedure Act Articles 33 and 201-2).

faqs.q: Can I postpone the date I have to appear?
faqs.a: If there are reasons such as arranging an interpreter, hiring a lawyer or departure plans, you can contact the investigator and ask to reschedule. However, if you keep failing to appear without a valid reason, an arrest warrant (체포영장) may be requested (Criminal Procedure Act Article 200-2), so do not avoid their calls.
