areaPages.title: Criminal Penalties and Your Stay
areaPages.lead: For foreigners, a criminal penalty does not end with a fine or a prison sentence. A sentence of imprisonment without labor or heavier is a ground for deportation, and even a fine is reflected in extension, change of status, permanent residency and naturalization reviews, so the level of the outcome and your stay must be considered together from the investigation stage.

seo.title: How Criminal Penalties Affect Foreigners' Stay in Korea: Drunk Driving, Voice Phishing, Drugs | Jisan Law Foreigner Center
seo.description: What happens to your stay in Korea when you receive a fine, a suspended sentence or a prison sentence: imprisonment without labor or heavier as a ground for deportation, cancellation of stay permits, standards for cancelling permanent residency, and the statutory penalties and responses for drunk driving, assault, drugs and providing bank accounts for voice phishing.
keywords: voice phishing bank account foreigner Korea

situations.title: When you should get advice
items: I was caught drunk driving and am worried about my visa extension
A fight broke out while drinking, and I was reported for assault
I lent my bank account and debit card for what I was told was a part-time job, and now I am told it was used for voice phishing
I am being investigated in a drug case because of something a friend gave me
I received a fine through a summary order (약식명령) and am considering whether to request a formal trial
I want to know whether I will be deported if I receive a suspended sentence

items.name: Immigration Act Article 46(1)(13) (Persons Subject to Deportation)
items.text: A person released after being sentenced to imprisonment without labor or a heavier sentence can be subject to deportation. For permanent residents, the scope is narrower, such as people released after being sentenced to 5 years or more of imprisonment with or without labor who fall under Ministry of Justice ordinance.

items.name: Immigration Act Article 89(1)(5) (Cancellation or Change of Permits)
items.text: If a violation of this Act or other laws is serious, a stay permit or other permit can be cancelled or changed.

items.name: Road Traffic Act Article 148-2(3) (Drunk Driving)
items.text: A blood alcohol concentration of 0.03 percent or more but less than 0.08 percent is punishable by imprisonment of up to 1 year or a fine of up to KRW 5 million; 0.08 percent or more but less than 0.2 percent by imprisonment of 1 to 2 years or a fine of KRW 5 million to 10 million; and 0.2 percent or more by imprisonment of 2 to 5 years or a fine of KRW 10 million to 20 million.

items.name: Electronic Financial Transactions Act Article 6(3) and Article 49(4) (Transferring or Lending Access Media)
items.text: Transferring access media such as bank accounts, debit cards or certificates, lending them in exchange for payment, or lending them knowing they will be used for a crime is punishable by imprisonment of up to 5 years or a fine of up to KRW 30 million.

table.title: Statutory Penalties for Cases Often Involving Foreigners
rows: Drunk driving (0.03 percent or more but less than 0.08 percent)
Imprisonment of up to 1 year or a fine of up to KRW 5 million

table.note: Based on laws in force as of October 2026. The statutory penalty is the range of punishment set by law, and the actual outcome depends on prior convictions, compensation to the victim, whether a settlement was reached and so on. In drug cases, the statutory penalty varies greatly depending on the type of drug and the act, so it must be checked separately.

sections.title: Each outcome affects your stay differently
body: A person released after being sentenced to imprisonment without labor or a heavier sentence can become subject to deportation. A typical case is being released after serving a prison sentence. Prison wardens must notify the immigration office when the release of a foreign inmate is decided (Immigration Act Article 84(2)). That is why some people are handed over to immigration on the day they finish their sentence.

A fine is not included in 'imprisonment without labor or a heavier sentence', which is a ground for deportation. However, if the violation is serious, your stay permit can be cancelled, and the fine is counted against you in extension, change of status, permanent residency and naturalization reviews. Obtaining an outcome that avoids or defers punishment, such as a suspended indictment (기소유예) or a suspended sentencing (선고유예), makes a big difference for your stay.

sections.title: Drunk driving and assault
body: Drunk driving is the most common type of case involving foreigners. If it is your first offense and the level is low, it often ends with a fine, but the fine record remains for immigration reviews. Refusing the breathalyzer test makes the punishment heavier, so do not refuse.

Assault is a crime that cannot be prosecuted if the victim does not want the offender punished. Settling with the victim can end the case, so it is important to try to apologize and settle early. However, if an injury results and the case becomes bodily injury, you can be punished even after settling.

sections.title: If you lent your bank account and became involved in voice phishing
body: Many foreigners are investigated after handing over their bank account, debit card or certificate because someone promised them a part-time job or a loan. Lending them in exchange for payment, or knowing they will be used for a crime, is in itself punishable by imprisonment of up to 5 years or a fine of up to KRW 30 million. If you also withdrew and delivered money, you may be treated more harshly as an accomplice or aider in fraud or telecommunications financial fraud.

In these cases, the key question is what you knew at the beginning. Preserve the job advertisement, chat messages, and the amount and timing of any money you received exactly as they are. Resetting your phone or deleting messages will only work against you.

sections.title: Drug cases and summary orders
body: Drug cases carry heavy penalties, and even use or possession alone can greatly affect your stay. Hair or urine tests and phone analysis are often carried out together, so it is important to decide on how you will give your statement before questioning.

Cases punishable by fines often end with a summary order (약식명령) without a trial. If you believe the amount of the summary order or the finding of guilt itself will cause problems for your stay, you can request a formal trial within 7 days of being notified (Criminal Procedure Act Article 453). The deadline is short, so check your mail as soon as you receive it.

factors.title: Circumstances that affect the outcome and the immigration decision
plus: Prior convictions of the same kind or previous immigration violations
Refusing a breathalyzer test, fleeing or deleting evidence
No compensation made to the victim at all
Signs of continued involvement in organized crime
minus: First offense, with circumstances worth considering in how it happened
Settlement with the victim and compensation for the harm
A record of steady work and tax payments in Korea
Korean family members and raising children
Cooperating with the investigation and giving truthful statements

steps.title: How the Jisan Law Foreigner Center responds

items.title: Calculating the effect on your stay
items.desc: For each possible outcome, we consider the chances of extension of stay, cancellation of your stay permit and deportation, and set our goal.

items.title: Preparing for and sitting in on questioning
items.desc: Through practice and sitting in on questioning, we help keep your statements consistent, and we check the interpreted statement record together.

items.title: Settlement and sentencing materials
items.desc: We work on a settlement with the victim's side, gather evidence of your work, family and life, and submit it with a written opinion.

items.title: Responding to summary orders and judgments
items.desc: If a summary order is issued, we decide whether to request a formal trial, and at trial we explain the effect on your stay as a sentencing factor.

items.title: Connecting to immigration procedures
items.desc: If the immigration office starts an investigation or issues a decision after the outcome, we continue on to statements of opinion, objections and administrative lawsuits.

faqs.q: Will I be deported if I receive a suspended sentence?
faqs.a: The ground for deportation is 'a person released after being sentenced to imprisonment without labor or a heavier sentence'. A suspended sentence is still a sentence of imprisonment, so this ground can become an issue, but the actual decision is made by the immigration office after looking at the case and your circumstances in Korea. If a suspended sentence is expected, your circumstances in Korea should be explained from the trial stage.

faqs.q: Once I pay the fine, is the immigration issue over?
faqs.a: Paying the fine and the immigration review are separate matters. Your criminal record will be reviewed at your next extension or change of status application, so prepare the judgment or summary order together with materials explaining how it happened and how you have lived since.

faqs.q: I only lent my bank account and did not receive any money. Can I still be punished?
faqs.a: Even if you did not receive payment, you can be punished if there are signs that you knew or could have known it would be used for a crime. How you were asked and what you were told become the issues, so do not delete your chat records, and get advice.

faqs.q: If I receive a suspended indictment, is there no problem with my stay?
faqs.a: A suspended indictment is not a criminal penalty, so it does not count as 'imprisonment without labor or a heavier sentence', which is a ground for deportation. However, a decision not to indict remains in investigation history records, and these can be checked when needed for a foreigner's stay or naturalization permit (Act on the Lapse of Criminal Sentences Article 2(6) and Article 6(1)(6)). Keep the decision and the settlement agreement so you can explain what happened at your next extension application.

areaPages.title: Criminal Complaints by Foreign Victims
areaPages.lead: Foreigners who are victims of crime can file a criminal complaint regardless of their nationality or visa status. If you are hesitating to report because of concerns about your stay, first check the rule under which public officials may be exempt from their duty to notify immigration when helping the victim comes first.

seo.title: Criminal Complaints by Foreign Crime Victims in Korea, Exemption from Immigration Reporting, Compensation Orders | Jisan Law Foreigner Center
seo.description: How foreigners in Korea can file a criminal complaint for assault, sexual crimes or fraud, interpreters and having a trusted person present, the exemption from the duty to notify immigration for victims with uncertain visa status, special extension rules for victims of domestic and sexual violence, compensation orders and crime victim relief payments.

situations.title: When you should get advice
items: I was hit at work, but I cannot report it because my period of stay has expired
I sent money for a secondhand item, but it never arrived and the seller stopped responding
I was sexually harassed by a manager at my company
Someone from my own country cheated me out of money I lent them
It is hard for me to write a criminal complaint in Korean
The offender's side keeps contacting me to settle

items.name: Criminal Procedure Act Articles 223 and 237 (Persons Entitled to File a Complaint; Form of Complaint)
items.text: A person harmed by a crime can file a criminal complaint, either in writing or orally, with a judicial police officer.

items.name: Immigration Act Article 84(1) proviso; Enforcement Decree Article 92-2; Enforcement Rules Article 70-2 (Exemption from the Duty to Notify)
items.text: Public officials who discover a person violating the Immigration Act must notify the immigration office. However, they may choose not to notify if they find that helping the victim must come first in duties such as investigating crimes like murder, bodily injury, assault, unlawful arrest or confinement, intimidation, sexual crimes, theft, robbery or fraud, or a labor inspector's investigation of unpaid wages.

items.name: Immigration Act Article 25-2 (Special Rules for Marriage Migrants, etc.)
items.text: A foreigner who has a trial, investigation or other legal remedy in progress because they were a victim of domestic violence, sexual violence, child abuse or human trafficking can be permitted to extend their period of stay until the procedure ends.

items.name: Act on Special Cases Concerning Expedition of Legal Proceedings Article 25 (Compensation Orders)
items.text: When a court convicts a defendant of certain crimes, such as bodily injury, sexual crimes, theft, fraud or embezzlement, it can, on the victim's application or on its own initiative, order compensation for direct property damage, medical expenses and emotional distress.

sections.title: You can file a complaint even if your visa status is uncertain
body: The right to file a criminal complaint does not depend on nationality or status of stay. Still, foreigners whose period of stay has expired hesitate to report because they fear being handed over to the immigration office if they go to the police station. The Immigration Act requires public officials to report violators they discover, but it makes an exception allowing them not to notify when helping the victim must come first, such as in a criminal investigation.

This exception applies to investigations of crimes such as assault, bodily injury, intimidation, confinement, sexual crimes, theft, robbery and fraud, and to a labor inspector's investigation of unpaid wages, among others. However, the official in charge decides whether to notify, so the outcome cannot be guaranteed. Get advice before reporting and decide on the order and method.

sections.title: Preparing the complaint and your statement
body: A complaint can be made orally, but if the case is complicated or your Korean is limited, it is more accurate to write the complaint in advance. Write down when, where, who and what happened in chronological order, and attach a list of evidence. You can also submit a written statement in a foreign language.

You can also ask for an interpreter when you are questioned as a victim. If you feel very anxious or tense about the questioning, you can ask for a person you trust to be present with you (Criminal Procedure Act Article 221(3) and Article 163-2). After giving your statement, listen to the record again through the interpreter before signing.

sections.title: Stay for victims of domestic or sexual violence
body: If an investigation or trial is in progress because you were a victim of domestic violence, sexual violence or human trafficking, there is a special rule that allows you to receive extensions of stay until the procedure ends. If needed for recovery from the harm, the stay can be extended even after that.
To use this special rule, you need documents showing that the case is actually in progress. Keep your complaint receipt, case number and court documents safe.

sections.title: How to recover your losses
body: If the offender is indicted, in some cases you can apply for a compensation order in the criminal trial and receive damages without a separate civil lawsuit. If you lost money, as in fraud cases, we also consider a provisional attachment (가압류) to freeze the offender's assets in advance.

If a crime victim dies or suffers a disability or serious injury and cannot receive compensation, there is a system under which the state pays crime victim relief money. Foreigners can receive it if they are nationals of a country with a reciprocal guarantee, or if they are, for example, the spouse of a Korean national and hold a specified status of stay such as permanent residency (Crime Victim Protection Act Article 23).

sections.title: You can file a complaint even if Korean is difficult for you
body: When a foreigner who is not fluent in Korean wants to file a complaint orally, the police must hear the statement through an interpreter and prepare a complainant statement record (Rules on Criminal Investigation Article 217(2)). If needed, you can also submit a written statement in a foreign language.

However, going through an interpreter takes a long time, and details are easily left out. Write down on paper in advance the details that must be accurate, such as dates, amounts and the other person's name, and bring it with you.

steps.title: How the Jisan Law Foreigner Center helps

items.title: Checking the case and your stay situation
items.desc: We check the harm you suffered together with your visa status, and first review the order of reporting and the possibility of exemption from the duty to notify.

items.title: Preserving evidence and writing the complaint
items.desc: We organize messages, money transfer records and medical certificates to write the criminal complaint, and prepare a written statement in a foreign language if needed.

items.title: Sitting in on victim questioning
items.desc: We go with you to the victim questioning and check the interpretation and the content of the statement record.

items.title: Settlement and compensation
items.desc: We review settlement offers from the offender's side, and pursue compensation orders, provisional attachments and civil lawsuits.

faqs.q: If I file a complaint, will I be handed over to the immigration office too?
faqs.a: If it is found that helping the victim comes first during a criminal investigation, the duty to notify can be waived. However, this depends on the official's judgment, so we cannot say it will definitely be waived. Organize your situation before reporting, and consider going with a representative.

faqs.q: Can I continue the case after I return to my home country?
faqs.a: If you appoint a lawyer as your representative, you can continue the criminal complaint and civil lawsuit even after leaving Korea. However, your statement as the victim may be needed again, so it is a good idea to give as much of your statement and evidence as possible before leaving.

faqs.q: If the offender offers me settlement money, can I accept it?
faqs.a: You can, but if the settlement agreement includes a statement that you do not want the offender punished (처벌불원), cases where the victim's wishes matter, such as assault, may end there. Check the amount, the payment method and the wording before signing.

areaPages.areaName: Unpaid Wages, Severance Pay and Workplace Injury
areaPages.title: Unpaid Wages, Severance Pay and Workplace Injury
areaPages.lead: Foreign workers are entitled to wages for the work they did, severance pay, and industrial accident insurance benefits if they are injured at work. Court precedent holds that even if you worked without work authorization, you can claim payment for the work you already did.

seo.title: Unpaid Wages, Severance Pay, Departure Guarantee Insurance and Workplace Injury for Foreign Workers in Korea | Jisan Law Foreigner Center
seo.description: Claiming unpaid wages and severance pay as a foreign worker in Korea, petitions to the Labor Office and civil lawsuits, the stricter unpaid wage penalties from October 8, 2026, the difference between Departure Guarantee Insurance and severance pay, industrial accident insurance for undocumented workers, and what to settle before leaving Korea.

situations.title: When you should get advice
items: I have not been paid for three months, and my boss just keeps asking me to wait
I received my Departure Guarantee Insurance payment, but it seems less than my severance pay
I injured my hand at the factory, and the company told me not to file an industrial accident claim
I worked after my period of stay expired, and I do not know whether I can ask for my wages
I have to leave Korea soon and am worried whether I can get the money owed to me
The company has closed and I cannot reach the owner

items.name: Labor Standards Act Articles 36, 43 and 107 (Settlement of Payments; Payment of Wages; Penalties)
items.text: When a worker leaves, wages and other payments must be made within 14 days, and wages must be paid directly, in full and in currency, at least once a month on a fixed date. From October 8, 2026, violations are punishable by imprisonment of up to 5 years or a fine of up to KRW 50 million, and cannot be prosecuted if the victim expressly does not want punishment (except for employers whose names have been publicly disclosed as delinquent).

items.name: Employee Retirement Benefit Security Act Articles 4, 8, 9 and 43
items.text: A worker who has worked continuously for 1 year or more, averaging 15 hours or more per week over 4 weeks, must be paid severance pay of at least 30 days' average wages for each year of service, within 14 days of leaving. Failure to pay is punishable by imprisonment of up to 5 years or a fine of up to KRW 50 million.

items.name: Act on the Employment of Foreign Workers Article 13 (Departure Guarantee Insurance and Trusts)
items.text: Employers who hire foreign workers must enroll in Departure Guarantee Insurance (출국만기보험) or a similar plan to pay severance, and the insurance money is paid within 14 days of departure (or within 14 days of the application date if applied for due to a change of status of stay or after departure). The right to claim expires if not exercised for 3 years.

items.name: Industrial Accident Compensation Insurance Act Articles 6 and 112
items.text: It applies to all businesses that employ workers (except some businesses specified by Presidential Decree), and the right to receive insurance benefits expires if not exercised for 3 years (5 years for disability and survivors' benefits, funeral expenses, etc.).

sections.title: You can claim wages even without a valid status of stay
body: The Supreme Court held that an employment contract made by a foreigner without work authorization is not automatically void, and that the worker can receive payment for work already done and industrial accident insurance benefits (Supreme Court Decision 94Nu12067, September 15, 1995). An employer refusing to pay wages because the worker has no status of stay is not justified.

If you file a petition with the Labor Office, a labor inspector investigates the facts. A labor inspector's investigation of unpaid wages is one of the duties in which the duty to notify immigration can be waived when helping the victim comes first (Enforcement Rules of the Immigration Act Article 70-2(5)). However, this requires the judgment of the official in charge, so get advice before filing a petition.

sections.title: Departure Guarantee Insurance and severance pay may not be the same amount
body: Severance pay for workers under the Employment Permit System is mainly paid through Departure Guarantee Insurance, to which the employer contributes monthly. Enrolling in this insurance is treated as setting up a severance pay system, but if the insurance payment is less than the severance pay calculated under the law, you need to consider whether you can claim the difference from the employer. Differences often arise when there was a lot of overtime or wages increased.

In principle, Departure Guarantee Insurance is paid within 14 days after departure, and the claim expires if not made within 3 years. Check the amount you will receive before leaving, and leave accurate bank account information.

sections.title: Steps to get the money owed to you
body: First, we calculate the amount owed using your employment contract, pay slips, attendance records and salary transfer records. Next, we file a petition with the regional employment and labor office to have the unpaid wages confirmed, and if the employer still does not pay, we create an enforceable basis through a civil lawsuit or a payment order (지급명령). If there is a risk that the company's assets will be moved, we first apply for a provisional attachment.

If the company has gone bankrupt or is found unable to pay, or if you have obtained a judgment ordering payment of unpaid wages, you can use the substitute payment system (대지급금), under which the state pays a certain range of wages on the employer's behalf (Wage Claim Guarantee Act Article 7).

From October 8, 2026, the penalty for employers who fail to pay wages and retirement payments became heavier: imprisonment of up to 5 years or a fine of up to KRW 50 million. For unpaid wages that arose before then, the provisions before the amendment may apply.

sections.title: If you were injured at work, start with an industrial accident claim
body: Industrial accident insurance applies to businesses that employ workers, regardless of the worker's status of stay. Even if the company blocks an industrial accident claim or suggests handling it privately as a company-paid injury (공상), the worker can apply directly to the Korea Workers' Compensation and Welfare Service (근로복지공단) for medical care benefits. Keep the contact details of coworkers who know what happened on the day of the injury, hospital records and photos.

During treatment, your departure schedule is the biggest worry. Being under treatment for a work-related injury is sometimes taken into account in extending your stay or calculating the workplace change period, so get advice together with your expiry date in mind.

steps.title: How the Jisan Law Foreigner Center handles your case

items.title: Calculating what you are owed
items.desc: Using documents, we calculate wages, overtime pay, severance pay and any shortfall in the Departure Guarantee Insurance payment.

items.title: Checking your stay schedule
items.desc: Based on your expiry date and planned departure date, we decide the order of the petition, lawsuit and provisional attachment.

items.title: Petition and accompanying you to appear
items.desc: We write the petition to the Labor Office and go with you when you are called in, helping with interpretation and your statement.

items.title: Lawsuit and enforcement
items.desc: If the employer does not pay, we bring a civil lawsuit, provisional attachment and compulsory enforcement, and help you apply for the substitute payment if needed.

items.title: Industrial accident claims and appeals
items.desc: We prepare the application for medical care benefits and the written account of the accident, and if it is not approved, we consider a request for review and an administrative lawsuit.

faqs.q: Can I get my unpaid wages even after I leave Korea?
faqs.a: If you appoint a representative, the lawsuit and enforcement can continue after you leave. However, it is much easier if you file the petition, have the unpaid wages confirmed and organize your bank account before leaving.

faqs.q: My boss wants me to sign a settlement saying I do not want him punished.
faqs.a: Unpaid wages is a crime that cannot be prosecuted if the victim does not want punishment. If you sign a statement that you do not want punishment (처벌불원서) before you have actually received all the money, you may lose your leverage, so sign it after payment is complete or clearly state the terms of installment payments.

faqs.q: Do I get no severance pay if I worked less than 1 year?
faqs.a: Severance pay arises when you have worked continuously for 1 year or more, averaging 15 hours or more per week over 4 weeks. If your contract was cut short and renewed repeatedly, we need to examine whether you actually worked continuously.

faqs.q: The company has closed and I cannot reach the owner.
faqs.a: If the company has gone bankrupt or is found unable to pay, or if you obtain a judgment or payment order for unpaid wages, you can apply for the substitute payment, under which the state pays a certain range of wages on the employer's behalf (Wage Claim Guarantee Act Article 7). First, file a petition with the Labor Office to have the unpaid wages confirmed.

areaPages.title: EPS (E-9) Workplace Change and Dismissal
areaPages.lead: Foreign workers under the Employment Permit System (고용허가제) can change workplaces only for specified reasons, and if they miss the application deadline, they may have to leave Korea. Even if the employer does not agree, in some cases you can apply for a change if the reason is not your fault.

seo.title: E-9 Workplace Change, Dismissal of Foreign Workers and Remedy Applications in Korea | Jisan Law Foreigner Center
seo.description: Reasons and number of times an Employment Permit System (E-9) worker can change workplaces, the 1-month deadline after the contract ends and the 3-month deadline after applying, changes without the employer's consent, applications for remedy for unfair dismissal, notice of dismissal and the re-employment system.

situations.title: When you should get advice
items: My wages keep coming late and I want to change companies, but my boss will not allow it
The dormitory conditions are so bad that I cannot stay there any longer
A manager verbally abused and assaulted me
I was suddenly told not to come to work from tomorrow
I applied to change workplaces and am worried I will not find a new company within 3 months
I have already changed workplaces three times and do not know whether I can change again

items.name: Act on the Employment of Foreign Workers Article 25 (Permission to Change Business or Workplace)
items.text: A worker can apply to change workplaces when, for example, the employer terminates the contract or refuses to renew it for a legitimate reason; the business suspends operations or closes; the employment permit is cancelled; hiring is restricted; dormitory standards are violated; or the Minister of Employment and Labor has announced that the worker cannot continue working for reasons that are not their fault, such as violations of working conditions or unfair treatment. If the worker does not obtain permission to change workplace within 3 months of applying, or does not apply within 1 month of the contract ending, they must leave Korea. In principle, changes cannot exceed 3 times in 3 years, or 2 times during the extended period, and changes for reasons that are not the worker's fault are not counted.

items.name: Act on the Employment of Foreign Workers Articles 18 and 18-2 (Period of Employment and Re-employment)
items.text: Foreign workers can work for up to 3 years from the date of entry, and if the employer requests permission for re-employment, the period can be extended once by less than 2 years.

items.name: Labor Standards Act Articles 23, 26 and 28 (Restrictions on Dismissal; Notice of Dismissal; Application for Remedy)
items.text: Workers cannot be dismissed without a justifiable reason (at workplaces with 5 or more regular employees), and to dismiss a worker, the employer must give 30 days' notice or pay at least 30 days' ordinary wages. A worker who is unfairly dismissed can apply to the Labor Relations Commission for remedy within 3 months of the date of dismissal.

sections.title: A workplace change requires a reason
body: Workers under the Employment Permit System cannot freely change companies whenever they want. They can apply to the Job Center (고용센터) for a workplace change only if there is a reason set by law. Typical reasons are the employer ending or not renewing the contract, the company suspending operations or closing, and reasons that are not the worker's fault, such as violations of working conditions or unfair treatment.

Reasons that are not the worker's fault are specified in a public notice by the Minister of Employment and Labor. You need to check whether circumstances such as unpaid wages, assault, sexual harassment or dormitory problems fall under the notice, and if they do, they give you grounds to apply for a change even without the employer's consent. Collect pay records, photos, medical certificates and messages that show the facts.

sections.title: If you miss the deadline, you may have to leave Korea
body: You must apply for a workplace change within 1 month of the date your employment contract with the employer ended. After applying, you must obtain permission to change workplace to a new workplace within 3 months. If these periods pass, you must leave Korea.

If you could not apply or obtain permission because of a work-related injury, illness, pregnancy or childbirth, the period starts again from the day that reason ends. If you are under treatment, be sure to keep a medical certificate and records of the treatment period.

sections.title: Counting the number of changes
body: In principle, you can change workplaces up to 3 times during the first 3 years and up to 2 times during a period extended by re-employment. However, changes for reasons that are not your fault are not counted. If you have already changed several times, checking the reasons for past changes may change the number of changes you have left.

sections.title: If you were suddenly dismissed
body: At a workplace with 5 or more regular employees, foreign workers also cannot be dismissed without a justifiable reason. The reason and timing of a dismissal must be given in writing, and if there was no 30 days' notice, you can receive 30 days' ordinary wages. If you believe the dismissal was unfair, apply to the Regional Labor Relations Commission for remedy within 3 months of the date of dismissal.

For workers under the Employment Permit System, dismissal is also tied to their stay. You must apply for a workplace change within 1 month of the date of dismissal, so the remedy application and the workplace change application need to be prepared together. Employers must report the dismissal of a foreign worker to the immigration office (Immigration Act Article 19), so also check that you have not been reported for workplace desertion (사업장 이탈).

sections.title: After the Labor Relations Commission decision
body: If you disagree with the Regional Labor Relations Commission's decision, you can apply to the National Labor Relations Commission for a review within 10 days of receiving the written decision, and if you disagree with the review decision, you can file an administrative lawsuit within 15 days of receiving it (Labor Standards Act Article 31). The deadlines are short, so decide the next step as soon as you receive a decision.

Your period of stay keeps running separately while the remedy procedure is in progress. You need to manage the workplace change application deadline and your expiry date together to avoid having to leave Korea even after obtaining a remedy.

steps.title: How the Jisan Law Foreigner Center helps

items.title: Checking the reasons and deadlines
items.desc: We check the date your contract ended, the time left on your stay, and the number of and reasons for your workplace changes so far.

items.title: Organizing evidence
items.desc: We gather materials showing unpaid wages or unfair treatment so that the reason for the change can be proven.

items.title: Change application and petition
items.desc: Along with the workplace change application at the Job Center, we decide whether a petition to the Labor Office or an application for remedy to the Labor Relations Commission is needed and proceed accordingly.

items.title: Connecting to immigration procedures
items.desc: We also take care of permission to change workplace, extension of stay and responding to workplace desertion reports.

faqs.q: If my boss will not agree to a workplace change, is there nothing I can do?
faqs.a: If it is hard to keep working for reasons that are not your fault, in some cases you can apply for a workplace change without the employer's consent. The key questions are whether the reason falls under the public notice and whether there is enough evidence.

faqs.q: Can I work somewhere else for a short time while I am between jobs?
faqs.a: Working somewhere else without permission to change workplace violates the Immigration Act and can lead to punishment and deportation. Do not work until you receive permission.

faqs.q: I heard I was reported for workplace desertion.
faqs.a: You need to organize the circumstances in which you actually stopped working and your contact records, and explain the facts to the Job Center and the immigration office. If the desertion report is untrue, it is important to correct it quickly.

areaPages.title: International Divorce, Custody and Inheritance
areaPages.lead: When spouses have different nationalities, the first question is which country's court will handle the divorce and which country's law applies. If you lived together in Korea or your child lives in Korea, the proceedings can usually be brought in a Korean court.

seo.title: International Divorce in Korea: Jurisdiction, Governing Law, Custody, Child Support and Inheritance of Korean Assets | Jisan Law Foreigner Center
seo.description: International jurisdiction of Korean courts and the governing law in divorces between foreign spouses or between a Korean and a foreigner, jurisdiction over custody and child support, Hague Convention procedures when a child is taken abroad, recognition of foreign judgments, and the law governing inheritance of assets left in Korea.

situations.title: When you should get advice
items: We are a foreign couple and want to know if we can divorce in Korea
I want to divorce my Korean husband and am worried whether the divorce will be recognized in my home country
My spouse took our child and went back to their home country
I want my home country's divorce judgment to be recognized in Korea
A family member who worked in Korea passed away, leaving savings and a housing deposit in Korea

items.name: Act on Private International Law Article 56 (Special Jurisdiction over Matrimonial Cases)
items.text: Korean courts have international jurisdiction in cases such as when one spouse's habitual residence is in Korea and the couple's last common habitual residence was in Korea, when the habitual residence of the plaintiff and all or some of the minor children is in Korea, or when both spouses are Korean nationals.

items.name: Act on Private International Law Articles 64 and 66 (General Effects of Marriage; Divorce)
items.text: Divorce is governed, in order, by the law of the spouses' common nationality, the law of their common habitual residence, and the law of the place most closely connected to them. However, if one spouse is a Korean national with habitual residence in Korea, Korean law applies.

items.name: Act on Private International Law Articles 59 and 60 (Jurisdiction over Parental Authority, Custody and Support Cases)
items.text: Korean courts have jurisdiction over cases concerning parental authority, custody and visitation of minor children if the child's habitual residence is in Korea, or if one parent and the child are Korean nationals. Korean courts have jurisdiction over support cases if the habitual residence of the person entitled to support is in Korea.

items.name: Act on Private International Law Articles 76 and 77 (Jurisdiction over Inheritance Cases; Law Governing Inheritance)
items.text: Korean courts have jurisdiction if the deceased's habitual residence at the time of death was in Korea or if inherited property is in Korea (unless its value is extremely small). Inheritance is governed by the law of the deceased's nationality at the time of death, but the deceased may designate by will the law of their habitual residence or the law of the place where real estate is located.

sections.title: Can you divorce in a Korean court?
body: If you lived together in Korea and one of you still lives in Korea, or if the person seeking the divorce and the child live in Korea, you can file for divorce in a Korean court. This is true even if the other spouse has returned to their home country.

If both spouses live abroad or have only weak ties to Korea, Korean courts may not have jurisdiction. Before filing, organize where the couple's life was based and where each of you lives now, and first confirm jurisdiction.

sections.title: Which country's law governs the divorce?
body: If there is a Korean spouse living in Korea, the divorce is governed by Korean law. For a foreign couple, it is governed by the law of their country if they share the same nationality, and otherwise by the law of the place where they live together, in that order. If a foreign couple of the same nationality divorces in Korea, the Korean court will apply the law of their home country.

Support after divorce follows the law that applied to the divorce. The relationship between parents and children is governed by the law of their nationality if the parents and child all share the same nationality, and otherwise by the law of the place where the child lives (Act on Private International Law Articles 72 and 73).

sections.title: Will the divorce be recognized in your home country?
body: Whether a Korean court's judgment is recognized in the other country depends on that country's law. Some countries do not recognize methods other than a court judgment, such as a divorce by agreement (협의이혼), so if you need to report the divorce in your home country, check the procedure in advance.

Conversely, for a foreign court's divorce judgment to be recognized in Korea, requirements such as the jurisdiction of that court, proper service of process, no violation of public order and reciprocity must be met (Civil Procedure Act Article 217).

sections.title: If a child has been taken abroad
body: If one parent took the child abroad without the other parent's consent, and both countries are parties to the Convention on the Civil Aspects of International Child Abduction (the Hague Convention), a procedure to seek the child's return can be used. Return cases for children brought to Korea are handled by the Seoul Family Court.

If more than 1 year has passed since the removal or retention and the child has settled into the new environment, return may be refused, so you must act quickly. If the child has not yet been taken out of Korea, we also consider applying to the family court for a pre-trial measure (사전처분) or a provisional injunction (가처분).

sections.title: Inheritance of assets left in Korea
body: When a foreigner who worked in Korea dies, inheritance is in principle governed by the law of the deceased's nationality. So you need to check that law to find out who the heirs are and what share each receives. To withdraw Korean bank deposits or a lease deposit, you often need to prepare documents from your home country proving who the heirs are, as required by Korean institutions, and have them translated and notarized.

Conversely, if a Korean national dies and some heirs are family members living abroad, inheritance follows the Korean Civil Act, and the deadline for renouncing the inheritance or accepting it with limited liability (3 months from the day the heir learned the inheritance began) also applies.

steps.title: How the Jisan Law Foreigner Center handles your case

items.title: Confirming jurisdiction and governing law
items.desc: We organize the nationalities and places of residence of the spouses and children and where they last lived together, and determine the jurisdiction of Korean courts and the law that applies.

items.title: Arranging service of process
items.desc: If the other spouse is abroad, we decide between service abroad and service by publication (공시송달), and prepare the necessary translations.

items.title: Divorce and custody lawsuit
items.desc: We claim divorce together with designation of the person with parental authority and the custodial parent, child support and division of property, and if your stay is at stake, we also argue over responsibility for the breakdown of the marriage.

items.title: Procedures after the judgment
items.desc: We follow through with the family relationship registration report, the documents needed to report the divorce in your home country, and enforcement of child support.

faqs.q: If the other spouse is in their home country, how is the complaint delivered?
faqs.a: It can be served at a foreign address, or if the address is unknown, by service by publication. Service abroad requires translation and takes time, so obtain the other spouse's address as accurately as possible.

faqs.q: Can I get child support from a spouse who lives abroad?
faqs.a: Child support can be set by a Korean judgment, but if the other spouse's assets are abroad, the judgment may need to be recognized and enforced in that country. If they have assets or a salary in Korea, we first consider enforcing against those.

faqs.q: Can a foreign couple divorce by agreement?
faqs.a: It depends on whether the applicable law of their home country recognizes divorce by agreement and whether a Korean divorce by agreement is effective in that country. If you need to report the divorce in your home country, it is often safer to proceed through a judgment or court mediation.

faqs.q: What happens to my status of stay if I divorce?
faqs.a: For a marriage migrant divorcing a Korean spouse, the way to keep your stay depends on who is mainly responsible for the breakdown of the marriage and whether you are raising a child. areaPages.lead: Once a foreigner completes alien registration and reports any change of residence, this has the same effect as a Korean move-in report (전입신고), so they are protected by the Housing Lease Protection Act. If your lease has ended and you have not received your deposit back, check an order for registration of lease rights (임차권등기명령) before you move out.

items.name: Immigration Act Article 88-2(2) (Relationship Between Residence Cards and Resident Registration Cards, etc.)
items.text: Alien registration and reports of change of residence under the Immigration Act replace resident registration and move-in reports.

items.name: Housing Lease Protection Act Articles 3 and 3-2 (Opposability; Recovery of Deposit)
items.text: Once you take possession of the house and complete resident registration, you can assert your lease against third parties from the next day. If you also have a fixed date stamp (확정일자) on the lease contract, you can recover your deposit in an auction or public sale before lower-ranking right holders.

items.name: Housing Lease Protection Act Article 3-3 (Order for Registration of Lease Rights)
items.text: If you do not get your deposit back after the lease ends, you can apply to the court where the house is located for an order for registration of lease rights.

sections.title: Foreign tenants are protected too
body: The Housing Lease Protection Act protects tenants from the day after they move into the house and complete resident registration. Foreigners complete alien registration instead of resident registration, and when they move, they report the change of residence within 15 days. The Immigration Act provides that this alien registration and report of change of residence replace resident registration and move-in reports.

If you delay reporting your change of residence after moving, you may not be protected during that period. If you get a fixed date stamp on your lease contract, you can recover your deposit ahead of others, according to priority, if the house goes to auction.

sections.title: What to check before moving out if you have not received your deposit
body: If your lease has ended and you move your registered residence elsewhere without getting your deposit back, you may lose protection for your current home. So it is safer to apply for an order for registration of lease rights before moving or leaving Korea, and move only after confirming that the registration has been made.

If the landlord still does not return the deposit, we demand its return by certified letter (내용증명) and bring a lawsuit for return of the deposit or seek a payment order. Once you obtain a judgment, you can put the house up for auction to recover your deposit.

sections.title: If you have to leave Korea
body: If your period of stay ends and you have to leave Korea while the deposit issue remains, you can appoint a representative and continue the proceedings after you leave. Before leaving, organize the lease registration, your bank account information and a power of attorney.

If a plaintiff with no address in Korea files a lawsuit, they may be ordered, at the other party's request, to provide security for litigation costs (Civil Procedure Act Article 117). If the amount is KRW 30 million or less, the case often proceeds relatively quickly under the small claims procedure.

sections.title: Contract disputes and fraud
body: Even if you signed a contract written in Korean, the contract does not become void simply because you did not understand its contents. However, if the other party deceived you about important terms, you can cancel the contract for fraud or claim damages. Keep conversations, advertisements and explanatory materials from before and after the contract.

If you sent money for a secondhand trade or an investment and the other person disappeared, you can file a criminal complaint for fraud. Fraud is punishable by imprisonment of up to 20 years or a fine of up to KRW 50 million (Criminal Act Article 347). To get your money back, we combine a criminal complaint with a provisional attachment on the other person's bank account or assets, and an application for a compensation order in the criminal trial.

sections.title: If the house has gone to auction
body: If you received documents saying an auction has started on the house you live in, first check the deadline for demanding distribution (배당요구 종기). People with priority rights to repayment, such as tenants with a fixed date stamp, must file a demand for distribution with the court to receive a distribution (Civil Execution Act Article 88). If you miss this date, you may not get your deposit back.

To receive the distribution, you must hand over the house to the person who bought it at auction (Housing Lease Protection Act Article 3-2(3)). If you are about to leave Korea, consider the auction schedule together with your stay schedule and appoint a representative.

steps.title: How the Jisan Law Foreigner Center handles your case

items.desc: We check your registered address, the date you reported your change of residence, the fixed date stamp and the property register to confirm where your deposit stands in priority.

items.desc: Before you move or leave Korea, we apply for an order for registration of lease rights and send a certified letter demanding return of the deposit.

items.title: Lawsuit and enforcement
items.desc: We proceed with a lawsuit for return of the deposit or a payment order, up to applying for an auction. After you leave, we continue as your representative.

faqs.q: Can foreigners get a fixed date stamp?
faqs.a: Yes. You can take your lease contract to a community service center (주민센터) or use the Internet Registry Office. It only has effect together with alien registration or a report of change of residence.

faqs.q: The landlord says he will return my deposit only after the next tenant moves in.
faqs.a: When the lease ends, the landlord is obliged to return the deposit, and finding a new tenant is the landlord's own matter. However, you should first check whether the lease was properly ended (for example, by giving notice that you will not renew).

faqs.q: If the lawsuit is decided after I leave Korea, how do I get the money?
faqs.a: Your representative can enforce the judgment and send the money received to your overseas bank account. Arrange a power of attorney and your overseas account information before leaving.

guides.stage: My visa extension or change of status was refused
guides.title: When your extension of stay or change of status is refused
guides.lead: If you have received a refusal notice (불허 통지서), first check the departure deadline. Filing an administrative appeal or lawsuit does not stop that deadline, so to challenge the refusal, you must also apply for a stay of execution within the deadline.

seo.title: What to Do After a Visa Extension Refusal Notice in Korea | Jisan Law Foreigner Center
seo.description: What to do right away and what not to do when your visa extension or change of status is refused in Korea, how the departure deadline is calculated, choosing between reapplying, an administrative appeal and a lawsuit, when to apply for a stay of execution, and how Jisan Law can help, step by step.
keywords: stay of execution visa refusal Korea

sections.title: What to do right now
body: Act in order from the day you received the notice. At this stage, securing the dates and documents comes first.
bullets: Write down the date you received the notice, and clearly mark the departure deadline on the notice in your calendar.
Take a photo of the reason for refusal stated in the notice, and if anything is unclear, ask the official in charge which requirement was lacking and write it down.
Gather copies of the documents you submitted with your application or your application history on HiKorea.
Start collecting documents that show why you should not have to leave, such as family, work, school or medical treatment schedules.
If the departure deadline is within 2 weeks, get advice right away. A decision on a stay of execution also takes time.

sections.title: What not to do
body: Acting in a hurry can make the later procedures harder.
bullets: Doing nothing until the departure deadline passes. Once the deadline passes, you will be overstaying and may face deportation or an immigration fine.
Thinking that you do not have to leave just because you filed a lawsuit. Without a decision granting a stay of execution, the decision remains in effect.
Reapplying right away with the same documents. If you do not fix the reason for refusal, the result is likely to be the same.
Making and submitting documents that are untrue. Submitting false documents is punishable and becomes a ground for cancelling your stay permit later.

sections.title: How the departure deadline is set
body: When the Ministry of Justice does not permit an extension or change of status, it states a departure deadline on the notice, which in principle is no later than 14 days from the notice's issue date (Enforcement Decree of the Immigration Act Article 33(2)). Sometimes the expiry date of your already-permitted period of stay is set as the departure deadline.

When a change of status of stay is refused, you may be allowed to keep staying under your original status of stay, and in that case the notice may not state a departure deadline. If you cannot leave within the deadline for an unavoidable reason such as illness or lack of transportation, you can apply to postpone the departure deadline (Enforcement Rules Article 33).

sections.title: What happens next
body: If the refusal was due to missing documents, adding them and reapplying may be the fastest route. If you believe the decision itself was wrong, choose an administrative appeal or administrative lawsuit. An administrative appeal is filed with the Central Administrative Appeals Commission and an administrative lawsuit with the Administrative Court, and the deadline for both is 90 days from the day you learned of the decision.

Either way, if a departure deadline applies, you must also apply for a stay of execution. In the application, state specifically the harm that would be hard to undo if you left, and support it with family relationship documents, medical certificates, or proof of enrollment or employment.

In the main case, we argue that the reason for refusal is factually wrong, or that even if it is correct, the decision is too harsh. Permission to change status of stay is at the authorities' discretion, but Supreme Court precedent holds that a decision based on a factual error or that violates the principle of proportionality is unlawful (Supreme Court Decision 2015Du48846, July 14, 2016).

sections.title: How Jisan Law can help
body: The Jisan Law Foreigner Center reviews your notice together with your application documents and first decides whether reapplying or challenging the decision is better. If we decide to challenge it, we prepare the administrative appeal, the complaint and the application for a stay of execution in time for the departure deadline, and then handle the additional evidence and the hearings. Consultations are available in English and Chinese.
If only a few days are left before your departure deadline, do not wait. Call us first at 02-6951-4097. We answer 24 hours a day, including weekends and public holidays.

faqs.q: The departure deadline on my notice has already passed.
faqs.a: If the deadline has passed, you are overstaying, which can lead to an investigation by the immigration office, an immigration fine or a decision such as a departure order. Get advice right away on whether the deadline for an administrative lawsuit (90 days from the day you learned of the decision) is still open and what procedures are available in your current situation.

faqs.q: Which is better, an administrative appeal or an administrative lawsuit?
faqs.a: An administrative appeal is relatively simple in cost and procedure, while an administrative lawsuit examines the facts and the law more thoroughly. You can also go straight to a lawsuit without an administrative appeal. The choice depends on the reason for refusal, the time left and the evidence you have ready.

faqs.q: I was refused because the company's documents came late. What if the company will not cooperate?
faqs.a: If your status of stay requires company documents, keep evidence showing that the company is not cooperating (such as messages requesting the documents). If there are also unpaid wages or unfair treatment, these should be addressed as labor issues as well.

guides.title: When you receive a departure order or deportation order
guides.lead: An objection to a deportation order (강제퇴거명령) must be filed within 7 days of receiving the order, and a departure order (출국명령) must be challenged within the set departure deadline. Start by checking the type of document you received and the dates.

seo.title: Departure Order or Deportation Order in Korea: 7-Day Objection and Administrative Lawsuit | Jisan Law Foreigner Center
seo.description: What to do right away and what not to do when you receive a departure order or deportation order in Korea, the 7-day objection and special permission to stay, lawsuits to cancel the order with a stay of execution, and entry restrictions after deportation, step by step.

sections.title: What to do right now
body: If you have received an order, start with the following today.
bullets: Check whether the title of the document you received is a departure recommendation (출국권고서), a departure order (출국명령서) or a deportation order (강제퇴거명령서).
Write down the date you received the order and the departure deadline. The 7 days for an objection to a deportation order are counted from the day you received it.
Take photos of the order, any earlier notices, your passport and your residence card, and send them to your family as well.
Write down the reasons you need to stay in Korea, such as Korean family members, children, illness, ongoing court cases or wages owed to you, and gather the related documents.
If you are not in a detention facility, be sure to follow any conditions set on reporting or where you live.

sections.title: What not to do
body: Mistakes at this stage can affect your ability to enter Korea again.
bullets: Cutting off contact or moving to hide. If it looks like you are fleeing, you will be detained, and it will also count against you in later decisions.

Missing the deadline in a departure order. If you do not leave by the deadline, a deportation order will be issued and your performance bond may be forfeited to the state (Immigration Act Article 68(4)).
Preparing your objection after the 7 days have passed.
Making up circumstances and submitting documents that are untrue.

sections.title: A departure order and a deportation order are different
body: A departure order is issued to people who have grounds for deportation but wish to leave voluntarily at their own expense, people whose stay permits have been cancelled, and others. The departure deadline is set within 30 days of the issue date, and you may be required to pay a performance bond of up to KRW 20 million.

A deportation order is a decision under which the state removes you directly. If you leave after receiving a deportation order, you may be banned from entering Korea until 5 years have passed (Immigration Act Article 11(1)(6)). So even though you leave either way, which decision you leave under makes a big difference for future entry.

sections.title: What happens next
body: You can file an objection to a deportation order with the Minister of Justice through the immigration office within 7 days of receiving the order. Even if the Minister of Justice finds the objection without merit, the Minister can permit you to stay if you previously held Korean nationality or have special reasons to stay (Article 61). The objection should state these special reasons together with evidence.

Separately from the objection, you can file an administrative lawsuit seeking cancellation of the departure order or deportation order within 90 days of the day you learned of the decision. If removal or the departure deadline is approaching, you must also apply for a stay of execution to remain in Korea during the lawsuit.

If the decision is upheld after you challenge it, you must leave. In that case, settle wages owed to you, deposits and ongoing cases before you leave. If you appoint a representative, these can be handled even after you leave.

sections.title: How Jisan Law can help
body: Jisan Law reviews the decision and the earlier investigation records and works out with you whether an objection, an administrative lawsuit or voluntary departure is the better option. We write the objection within 7 days, and if a lawsuit and stay of execution are needed, we proceed with them right away. If you are in a detention facility, we visit you to hear your circumstances directly and arrange an interpreter if needed.
The deadline for an objection is short. If you have received an order, contact us first at 02-6951-4097. We answer 24 hours a day, including weekends and public holidays.

faqs.q: Does a departure order also come with an entry ban?
faqs.a: Unlike a deportation order, the law does not set a specific number of years of entry ban for a departure order. However, depending on the violation that led to the departure order, entry may be restricted for a certain period, so this must be checked separately based on the reasons for the decision.

faqs.q: If I file an objection, will I not be removed until the result comes out?
faqs.a: There is no specific rule that filing an objection alone stops removal. If removal is imminent, you should also consider filing an administrative lawsuit with an application for a stay of execution.

faqs.q: Can I ask for a departure order instead of deportation?
faqs.a: Even where there are grounds for deportation, a departure order can be issued to a person who wishes to leave voluntarily at their own expense (Immigration Act Article 68(1)(1)). Before a decision is made, you can request this, and it is an important difference when you think about entering Korea in the future.

guides.stage: My family member is held in an immigration detention center
guides.title: When a family member is held in an immigration detention center
guides.lead: If a family member was moved to an immigration detention center (외국인보호소) or a holding room after a crackdown or after release from prison, first find out where and why they are being held. Detention has set time limits and procedures, and you can request a review and apply for temporary release to the Immigration Detention Committee (외국인보호위원회).

seo.title: What to Do When a Family Member Is in Immigration Detention in Korea: Temporary Release | Jisan Law Foreigner Center
seo.description: When a foreign family member is held in an immigration detention center in Korea after a crackdown or release from prison: checking the detention notice, family visits and lawyer visits, detention periods, review requests and applications for temporary release to the Immigration Detention Committee, and preparing the deposit and a guarantor, step by step.

sections.title: What to do right now
body: If you have been told that your family member is being held, organize things in the following order.
bullets: Check whether you received a detention notice. When someone is detained, immigration officers must inform their family or others in writing within 3 days of the date, place and reason for detention.
Confirm the place of detention (which immigration office's holding room, or which immigration detention center) and the contact details of the department in charge.
Gather information on where your family member's passport is, their alien registration number, their status of stay, and documents showing family relationships with Koreans.
If your family member has ongoing court cases, unpaid wages or an illness under treatment, gather the related documents separately.
Decide who can act as a guarantor and an address where they can stay.

sections.title: What not to do
body: What is said and signed during detention is used as is in later procedures.
bullets: Encouraging your family member to sign documents they do not understand.
Thinking that refusing to cooperate with removal will lead to faster release. Not cooperating with removal can be a reason to extend detention (Immigration Act Article 63(2)).
Thinking that preparing the deposit is all you need. Temporary release is decided by looking at the reasons and the evidence.
Believing a broker who promises to get them out in exchange for money.

sections.title: Detention has set time limits
body: Detention to review whether a person is subject to deportation is limited to 10 days, and can be extended once by another 10 days if unavoidable. If, after a deportation order, the person cannot be removed immediately because they have no passport or transportation, they can be detained for up to 2 months.

Under the amendment in force since June 2025, detention beyond 2 months can only be extended 3 months at a time with the approval of the Immigration Detention Committee. The total detention period in principle cannot exceed 9 months, and even in exceptional cases such as refugee lawsuits or serious crimes, it cannot exceed 20 months. Once the limit is exceeded, the person must be released immediately (Articles 63 and 63-2). Before applying for approval to extend, the person must be given a chance to state their opinion (Article 66-3).

sections.title: What happens next
body: If you object to the detention itself, you can request a review of the detention by the Immigration Detention Committee. The Committee must decide within 3 weeks of receiving the documents, and can extend this once by up to 2 weeks if unavoidable.

If there are specific reasons for release, apply for temporary release from detention. Not only the detained person but also a guarantor or family member can apply, and the application should be accompanied by evidence explaining the reasons and showing the ability to pay the deposit. If release is granted, a deposit of up to KRW 20 million must be paid and conditions such as restrictions on residence and regular reporting must be followed.

If a deportation order has been issued, you should also consider an objection within 7 days of receiving the order and an administrative lawsuit within 90 days. Detention and deportation are separate decisions, and each is challenged in a different way.

sections.title: How Jisan Law can help
body: Jisan Law visits the detention facility to hear the person's circumstances directly and checks how the detention happened and the related documents. We write the review request and the application for temporary release together with supporting evidence, and if an objection to a deportation order or an administrative lawsuit is needed, we continue with those. We can consult with the family in English or Chinese, and arrange an interpreter if needed.
The first few days after detention are important. If your family member has been detained, let us know first at 02-6951-4097. We answer 24 hours a day, including weekends and public holidays.

faqs.q: Will the deposit be returned later?
faqs.a: If the conditions of temporary release are followed, the deposit is returned through the refund procedure. If the conditions are broken, for example by fleeing or ignoring an order to appear without a valid reason, the temporary release can be cancelled and all or part of the deposit may be forfeited to the state (Immigration Act Article 66).

faqs.q: Can we ask for the consulate to be informed?
faqs.a: If the detained person wishes, immigration officers must inform that country's consul of the date, place and reason for detention, unless there are urgent circumstances (Immigration Act Article 54(2)).

faqs.q: My detained family member was not paid wages. What can we do?
faqs.a: Payment for work done can be claimed regardless of status of stay. Even during detention or after removal, a petition to the Labor Office and a lawsuit can continue through a representative, so the family should first secure the employment contract and bank statements.

guides.stage: The police asked me to come in for questioning
guides.title: When a foreigner is asked to appear at the police
guides.lead: If the police have asked you to appear as a suspect, prepare your interpreter and how you will give your statement before questioning. For foreigners, the outcome carries over to immigration reviews, so you need to be careful from the very first questioning.

seo.title: Asked to Appear at the Police as a Foreigner in Korea: Interpreters and Preparing for Questioning | Jisan Law Foreigner Center
seo.description: What a foreigner should do right away when asked to appear at the police in Korea, how to request an interpreter, checking the statement record, rescheduling the date, what not to do, referral and decisions after questioning, the effect on your stay, and how Jisan Law sits in on questioning.

sections.title: What to do right now
body: If you received a text or call asking you to appear, check the following before setting a date.
bullets: Find out and write down which police station and which investigator is calling you, and for what case (offense).
Tell the investigator in advance that you need an interpreter and in which language.
Check your passport and residence card and note your status of stay, its expiry date and any planned departure.
Do not delete messages, photos or money transfer records related to the case. Keep them as they are.
If you want to go with a lawyer, get advice before setting the date to appear.

sections.title: What not to do
body: Your statement at the first questioning is kept in the statement record and becomes the basic material for later decisions.
bullets: Being questioned without an interpreter because you can roughly understand Korean.
Signing a statement record you do not understand.
Filling in what you cannot remember with guesses.
Going to see or contacting the victim directly to pressure them to settle. This can be mistaken for intimidation or destroying evidence.
Ignoring the request to appear and cutting off contact. An arrest warrant may be requested.

sections.title: Interpretation and checking the statement record
body: When the police question a foreigner, they must provide interpretation in a language the person understands (Police Investigation Rules Article 91(1)). If the record was prepared through an interpreter, the police must note in the record that it was read to you through the interpreter and obtain the interpreter's signature.

When the questioning ends, ask the interpreter to read the record to you again from the beginning. If anything differs from what you said, ask for it to be corrected, and check that your request was noted in the record. If you are tired or do not understand, you can ask for a break.

sections.title: What happens next
body: When the police questioning ends, the police either refer the case to prosecutors (송치) or decide not to refer it (불송치). From October 2, 2026, the Prosecutors' Office is abolished, and the Public Prosecution Service (공소청) decides whether to indict. Prosecutors do not investigate directly. They decide based on the case files and request supplementary investigation if needed. This makes the statements and materials submitted at the police stage all the more important.

Minor cases often end with a fine set by a summary order (약식명령). If you receive a summary order, you can request a formal trial within 7 days. The outcome is reflected in reviews for extension of stay, change of status of stay, permanent residency and naturalization, so we aim for an outcome that avoids punishment, such as a suspended indictment, and prepare evidence of compensation to the victim and of your life in Korea.
You may be banned from leaving Korea while an investigation or trial is ongoing. If you have plans to leave, tell the investigator in advance and arrange the questioning schedule.

sections.title: How Jisan Law can help
body: At Jisan Law, a managing partner advises you personally, and we practice the questioning in advance with likely questions. A lawyer goes into the questioning with you, checks that the interpreted questions and answers match, and objects on the spot to leading or improper questions. After the questioning, we submit defense counsel's written opinion and also prepare for how the outcome will affect your stay. Consultations are available in English and Chinese.
If a date for questioning has been set, contact us at 02-6951-4097 before you appear.

faqs.q: They say they are calling me as a witness (참고인). Do I need a lawyer?
faqs.a: Even a witness can become a suspect during questioning. If your role in the case is unclear or money changed hands, get advice before you appear.

faqs.q: What if the interpreter seems to be translating my words differently?
faqs.a: Ask for it to be interpreted again on the spot, and request a correction when you check the statement record. If you raise an objection, it must be added to the record (Criminal Procedure Act Article 244(2)).

faqs.q: Will immigration be informed as soon as I am questioned?
faqs.a: Public officials who discover a person violating the Immigration Act in the course of their duties must notify the immigration office (Immigration Act Article 84). If there is no problem with your status of stay, questioning alone will not change your stay, but the outcome may be reflected in later reviews.
